terms.simpleDefinition: Visible or measurable swelling of the abdomen from gas, fluid (ascites), faeces, mass, or pregnancy.
terms.definition: Visible or measurable swelling of the abdomen from gas, fluid (ascites), faeces, mass, or pregnancy.
terms.clinicalContext: Measure abdominal girth consistently at umbilical level, auscultate all four quadrants for bowel sounds before palpation, and assess rigidity or guarding.

terms.simpleDefinition: Abnormal vaginal discharge is defined as discharge that is different from usual with respect to colour/odour/consistency (e.g. discoloured or purulent or
terms.definition: Abnormal vaginal discharge is defined as discharge that is different from usual with respect to colour/odour/consistency (e.g. discoloured or purulent or (Gynecology & Reproductive health curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Women with vaginal discharge should be managed according to the flow chart. The flow chart differentiates between candidiasis and other vaginal discharges.

terms.simpleDefinition: Abortion is defined as the expulsion of products of conception before 28 weeks of gestation.
terms.definition: Abortion is defined as the expulsion of products of conception before 28 weeks of gestation. (Gynecology & Reproductive health curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Health educate the community about the dangers of unsafe abortion.

terms.simpleDefinition: Premature separation of a normally implanted placenta from the uterine wall after 20 weeks gestation.
terms.definition: An obstetric emergency presenting with painful dark vaginal bleeding, tense 'woody' tender uterus, uterine hypertonus, and acute foetal distress or demise.
terms.clinicalContext: NEVER perform digital vaginal examination until placenta praevia is excluded; establish two wide-bore 16G/18G IV lines, cross-match blood urgently, and prepare for emergency delivery.
terms.mnemonics: Abruption = Acute painful + Board-like uterus.

terms.simpleDefinition: Localized painful fluctuant collection of pus walled off inside body tissues following bacterial invasion.
terms.definition: Localized painful fluctuant collection of pus walled off inside body tissues following bacterial invasion.
terms.clinicalContext: Treat with surgical Incision & Drainage (I&D) plus sterile moist packing — antibiotics alone cannot penetrate thick abscess capsules cleanly.

terms.simpleDefinition: Absorption & Distribution describes what the body does to a medicine after administration. The nurse should connect absorption, distribution, metabolism and elimination with route selection, dose timing, organ function.
terms.definition: Absorption & Distribution describes what the body does to a medicine after administration. The nurse should connect absorption, distribution, metabolism and elimination with route selection, dose timing, organ function. (Pharmacology I curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Absorption & Distribution describes what the body does to a medicine after administration. The nurse should connect absorption, distribution, metabolism and elimination with route selection, dose timing, organ function.

terms.simpleDefinition: Abnormally low arterial carbon dioxide level (hypocapnia) typically triggered by hyperventilation.
terms.definition: Abnormally low arterial carbon dioxide level (hypocapnia) typically triggered by hyperventilation.
terms.clinicalContext: Coach anxious hyperventilating patients on slow pursed-lip breathing and check underlying hypoxia, pain, or metabolic acidosis before attributing to anxiety.

terms.simpleDefinition: Cup-shaped socket of the pelvic hip bone articulating with the femoral head.
terms.definition: Cup-shaped socket of the pelvic hip bone articulating with the femoral head.
terms.clinicalContext: Assess hip alignment, limb shortening, and external rotation urgently after pelvic falls or RTA trauma.

terms.simpleDefinition: Acute liver centrilobular necrosis caused by NAPQI metabolite accumulation after overdose (> 150 mg/kg or > 7.5–10 g adult).
terms.definition: Acute liver centrilobular necrosis caused by NAPQI metabolite accumulation after overdose (> 150 mg/kg or > 7.5–10 g adult).
terms.clinicalContext: Administer N-Acetylcysteine (NAC) IV/oral antidote urgently — most effective within 8 hours of ingestion; check 4-hour serum paracetamol level & LFTs.

terms.simpleDefinition: Oesophageal motility disorder with failure of lower oesophageal sphincter relaxation and absent peristalsis.
terms.definition: Oesophageal motility disorder with failure of lower oesophageal sphincter relaxation and absent peristalsis.
terms.clinicalContext: Elevate head during meals, encourage small soft swallows with fluids, and monitor for aspiration pneumonia.

terms.simpleDefinition: Blood pH below 7.35 caused either by bicarbonate loss/acid accumulation or CO2 retention.
terms.definition: Blood pH below 7.35 caused either by bicarbonate loss/acid accumulation or CO2 retention.
terms.clinicalContext: Track arterial blood gases (pH, PaCO2, HCO3-), Kussmaul hyperventilation, serum potassium shifts, and underlying DKA, shock, or COPD.

terms.simpleDefinition: Progressive enlargement of extremities and facial bones in adults from excess Growth Hormone (pituitary adenoma).
terms.definition: Progressive enlargement of extremities and facial bones in adults from excess Growth Hormone (pituitary adenoma).
terms.clinicalContext: Assess visual field deficits (bitemporal hemianopia), hypertension, sleep apnoea, and glucose intolerance.

terms.simpleDefinition: Acromegaly and Gigantism are conditions that result from hyperpituitarism, which is the excessive secretion of growth hormone (GH) by the pituitary gland.
terms.definition: Acromegaly and Gigantism are conditions that result from hyperpituitarism, which is the excessive secretion of growth hormone (GH) by the pituitary gland. (Medical Nursing (III) curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Enlarged hands, feet, and facial features (jaw, nose, forehead)

terms.simpleDefinition: Traumatic disruption of AC ligaments connecting distal clavicle and acromion after direct lateral shoulder fall.
terms.definition: Traumatic disruption of AC ligaments connecting distal clavicle and acromion after direct lateral shoulder fall.
terms.clinicalContext: Support injured arm comfortably in broad arm sling, apply ice intermittently, assess distal radial pulse/sensory axillary nerve over deltoid.

terms.simpleDefinition: Premalignant rough scaly macule/papule on chronically sun-exposed skin especially in fair skin or albinism.
terms.definition: Premalignant rough scaly macule/papule on chronically sun-exposed skin especially in fair skin or albinism.
terms.clinicalContext: Counsel broad-spectrum sunscreen, protective hats/clothing (crucial for Ugandans with oculocutaneous albinism), and dermatology cryotherapy.

terms.simpleDefinition: Spectrum covering Unstable Angina, NSTEMI, and STEMI resulting from coronary plaque erosion/rupture.
terms.definition: Spectrum covering Unstable Angina, NSTEMI, and STEMI resulting from coronary plaque erosion/rupture.
terms.clinicalContext: Record 12-lead ECG within 10 minutes of arrival, check serial Troponin-I/T, give chewed Aspirin 300 mg + dual antiplatelet per clinician order.

terms.simpleDefinition: Acute Glomerulonephritis (AGN)
terms.definition: Acute Glomerulonephritis (AGN) (Surgical Nursing III and Paediatric Nursing (II) curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Use Acute Glomerulonephritis as a practical nursing topic, not only a memorized definition. Prioritize airway, breathing, circulation, pain, asepsis, wound healing and early complication detection.

terms.simpleDefinition: Sudden reversible decline in glomerular filtration rate causing rising creatinine, urea, and oliguria.
terms.definition: Sudden reversible decline in glomerular filtration rate causing rising creatinine, urea, and oliguria.
terms.clinicalContext: Calculate strict hourly urine output (< 0.5 mL/kg/hr alert), hold nephrotoxic drugs (gentamicin/NSAIDs), and monitor ECG for hyperkalaemia.

terms.simpleDefinition: Primary chronic adrenal cortex insufficiency causing deficient cortisol and aldosterone.
terms.definition: Primary chronic adrenal cortex insufficiency causing deficient cortisol and aldosterone.
terms.clinicalContext: Educate patients never to stop oral Hydrocortisone abruptly and double doses during fever/stress to prevent fatal Addisonian crisis.

terms.simpleDefinition: Addison's disease, also known as primary adrenal insufficiency, is a rare disorder characterized by the insufficient production of hormones by the adrenal
terms.definition: Addison's disease, also known as primary adrenal insufficiency, is a rare disorder characterized by the insufficient production of hormones by the adrenal (Medical Nursing (III) curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: One of the potential complications of Addison’s Disease is renal failure, which refers to the loss of kidney function.

terms.simpleDefinition: Adduction moves a limb toward the body midline; abduction moves a limb away from the midline.
terms.definition: Adduction moves a limb toward the body midline; abduction moves a limb away from the midline.
terms.clinicalContext: Maintain hip abduction with a triangular pillow after total hip arthroplasty per orthopaedic orders to prevent dislocation.

terms.simpleDefinition: Malignant epithelial tumour originating in glandular or secretory tissues such as stomach, colon, lung, or breast.
terms.definition: Malignant epithelial tumour originating in glandular or secretory tissues such as stomach, colon, lung, or breast.
terms.clinicalContext: Coordinate analgesia, nutrition support, staging investigations, and compassionate patient/family counselling.

terms.simpleDefinition: Post-operative airway vigilance after lymphoid pharyngeal excision.
terms.definition: Post-operative airway vigilance after lymphoid pharyngeal excision.
terms.clinicalContext: Position side-lying/prone during recovery, watch frequent swallowing (silent hidden pharyngeal bleeding red alert!), avoid red liquids & harsh coughing.

terms.simpleDefinition: Fibrous scar bands forming between internal tissues and organs after abdominal surgery or PID.
terms.definition: Fibrous scar bands forming between internal tissues and organs after abdominal surgery or PID.
terms.clinicalContext: Monitor post-op bowel obstruction red flags: colicky pain, bilious vomiting, distension, and absent flatus.

terms.simpleDefinition: We take medications or drugs to diagnose, treat or prevent illness.
terms.definition: We take medications or drugs to diagnose, treat or prevent illness. (Foundations of nursing II, Sociology and psychology curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Drug administration is a safety procedure, not just giving tablets or injections. The nurse protects the patient by verifying the order, patient, medicine, dose, route, time, indication, allergies, response and.

terms.simpleDefinition: Adolescent-friendly health services refer to those services that are geographically accessible, affordable, acceptable, welcoming, and provide confidentiality
terms.definition: Adolescent-friendly health services refer to those services that are geographically accessible, affordable, acceptable, welcoming, and provide confidentiality (Gynecology & Reproductive health curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Use Adolescent friendly health services as a practical nursing topic, not only a memorized definition. Start with normal structure and function, then connect it to assessment findings and disease.

terms.simpleDefinition: Adolescent Reproductive Health (ARH) is a state of complete physical, mental and social well being and not merely the absence of disease or infirmity, in all
terms.definition: Adolescent Reproductive Health (ARH) is a state of complete physical, mental and social well being and not merely the absence of disease or infirmity, in all (Gynecology & Reproductive health curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Health Education : Providing comprehensive health education to adolescents, addressing major concerns such as HIV/AIDS and pregnancies.

terms.simpleDefinition: Adolescent sexuality is a stage of human development in which adolescents experience and explore sexual feelings.
terms.definition: Adolescent sexuality is a stage of human development in which adolescents experience and explore sexual feelings. (Gynecology & Reproductive health curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Use Adolescent Sexuality as a practical nursing topic, not only a memorized definition. Start with normal structure and function, then connect it to assessment findings and disease.

terms.simpleDefinition: Potent alpha/beta adrenergic agonist used first-line in anaphylaxis and cardiac arrest resuscitation.
terms.definition: Potent alpha/beta adrenergic agonist used first-line in anaphylaxis and cardiac arrest resuscitation.
terms.clinicalContext: Administer 0.5 mg (1:1000) IM into outer thigh immediately for anaphylaxis; use 1 mg (1:10,000) IV during cardiac arrest algorithms.

terms.simpleDefinition: An advance directive, also known as an Advance Directive, is a legal document that upholds the principle of autonomy by expressing a patient's desires
terms.definition: An advance directive, also known as an Advance Directive, is a legal document that upholds the principle of autonomy by expressing a patient's desires (Palliative Care Nursing curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Use Advanced directives as a practical nursing topic, not only a memorized definition. Focus on comfort, dignity, symptom control, communication and family support.

terms.simpleDefinition: Adverse Drug Effects describes what the body does to a medicine after administration. The nurse should connect absorption, distribution, metabolism and elimination with route selection, dose timing, organ function and.
terms.definition: Adverse Drug Effects describes what the body does to a medicine after administration. The nurse should connect absorption, distribution, metabolism and elimination with route selection, dose timing, organ function and. (Pharmacology I curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Adverse Drug Effects describes what the body does to a medicine after administration. The nurse should connect absorption, distribution, metabolism and elimination with route selection, dose timing, organ function and.

terms.simpleDefinition: Adverse reactions explained for mental-health nursing with medicine-safety checks, risk monitoring, adherence teaching and legal documentation priorities.
terms.definition: Adverse reactions explained for mental-health nursing with medicine-safety checks, risk monitoring, adherence teaching and legal documentation priorities. (Mental Health Nursing(II) Pharmacology (III) curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Adverse reactions explains how a medicine produces its effect at receptors, enzymes, ion channels or other body targets. Nursing care links the expected action to measurable patient outcomes and early recognition of.

terms.simpleDefinition: Aetiological factors of mental illness is a psychiatric nursing topic that links mental status, behaviour, emotions, thought patterns, relationships and daily function. The nurse supports safety, therapeutic.
terms.definition: Aetiological factors of mental illness is a psychiatric nursing topic that links mental status, behaviour, emotions, thought patterns, relationships and daily function. The nurse supports safety, therapeutic. (Mental Health Nursing (I) and Pharmacology (II) curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Aetiological factors of mental illness is a psychiatric nursing topic that links mental status, behaviour, emotions, thought patterns, relationships and daily function. The nurse supports safety, therapeutic.

terms.simpleDefinition: Absence of fever (normal body temperature around 36.2 C–37.4 C).
terms.definition: Absence of fever (normal body temperature around 36.2 C–37.4 C).
terms.clinicalContext: Note that malnourished or severely immunocompromised neonates/elderly can have lethal sepsis while remaining afebrile.

terms.simpleDefinition: Painful intermittent cramping uterine contractions during the first days postpartum caused by breastfeeding oxytocin release especially in multiparae.
terms.definition: Painful intermittent cramping uterine contractions during the first days postpartum caused by breastfeeding oxytocin release especially in multiparae.
terms.clinicalContext: Reassure mother that afterpains confirm healthy uterine involution; keep bladder empty and offer safe Paracetamol/Ibuprofen 30 min prior to feeds.

terms.simpleDefinition: Intense anxiety about public open or enclosed spaces where escape or help feels difficult.
terms.definition: Intense anxiety about public open or enclosed spaces where escape or help feels difficult.
terms.clinicalContext: Use calm graded desensitization, slow diaphragmatic breathing, and avoid abrupt forceful confrontation.

terms.simpleDefinition: Dangerously severe deficiency of granulocytes (neutrophils), carrying extreme bacterial sepsis risk.
terms.definition: Dangerously severe deficiency of granulocytes (neutrophils), carrying extreme bacterial sepsis risk.
terms.clinicalContext: Institute protective reverse isolation, avoid rectal temperatures/enemas, and treat any fever >= 38 C as an immediate emergency.

terms.simpleDefinition: The passage that allows air to move into and out of the lungs.
terms.definition: The airway includes the nose, mouth, throat, larynx, trachea and bronchi. A clear airway is essential for breathing.
terms.clinicalContext: Airway assessment is a first nursing priority. Obstruction, secretions, vomiting or reduced consciousness can quickly become life-threatening.
terms.example: In practice, nurses use the term airway when assessing, documenting or explaining patient care.
terms.mnemonics: Connect the word to assessment, documentation and safe nursing action.

terms.simpleDefinition: Extrapyramidal antipsychotic side-effect causing intense subjective inner restlessness and pacing.
terms.definition: Extrapyramidal antipsychotic side-effect causing intense subjective inner restlessness and pacing.
terms.clinicalContext: Distinguish carefully from worsening psychosis before increasing antipsychotic doses; review with prescriber for dose reduction or beta-blocker/anticholinergic relief.

terms.simpleDefinition: Major plasma protein synthesized by liver (Normal 35–50 g/L) maintaining intravascular colloid oncotic pull.
terms.definition: Major plasma protein synthesized by liver (Normal 35–50 g/L) maintaining intravascular colloid oncotic pull.
terms.clinicalContext: Low albumin (nephrotic syndrome, liver failure, kwashiorkor) leaks water directly into third spaces creating pitting oedema & ascites.

terms.simpleDefinition: Presence of abnormal albumin protein in urine, indicating glomerular barrier damage or pre-eclampsia.
terms.definition: Presence of abnormal albumin protein in urine, indicating glomerular barrier damage or pre-eclampsia.
terms.clinicalContext: Check urine dipstick protein at every antenatal visit >= 20 weeks alongside blood pressure screening.

terms.simpleDefinition: Alcohol Abuse is a mental-health and safety topic because substance use or poisoning can affect judgement, behaviour, breathing, circulation, family wellbeing and long-term recovery.
terms.definition: Alcohol Abuse is a mental-health and safety topic because substance use or poisoning can affect judgement, behaviour, breathing, circulation, family wellbeing and long-term recovery. (Mental Health Nursing(II) Pharmacology (III) curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Alcohol Abuse is a mental-health and safety topic because substance use or poisoning can affect judgement, behaviour, breathing, circulation, family wellbeing and long-term recovery.

terms.simpleDefinition: Severe sympathetic rebound 48–96 hrs post cessation: coarse tremor, hallucinations, tachycardia, hypertension, fever, and seizures.
terms.definition: Severe sympathetic rebound 48–96 hrs post cessation: coarse tremor, hallucinations, tachycardia, hypertension, fever, and seizures.
terms.clinicalContext: Start CIWA-Ar monitoring, give Diazepam/Chlordiazepoxide symptom-triggered sedation AND IV Thiamine BEFORE any glucose.

terms.simpleDefinition: Arterial pH > 7.45 from excess bicarbonate retention, protracted gastric vomiting, or hyperventilation.
terms.definition: Arterial pH > 7.45 from excess bicarbonate retention, protracted gastric vomiting, or hyperventilation.
terms.clinicalContext: Monitor for circumoral numbness, carpopedal spasm (hypocalcaemic tetany), and hypokalaemia.

terms.simpleDefinition: Xanthine oxidase inhibitor lowering uric acid chronically to prevent recurrent gout flares and uric acid nephropathy.
terms.definition: Xanthine oxidase inhibitor lowering uric acid chronically to prevent recurrent gout flares and uric acid nephropathy.
terms.clinicalContext: Never initiate abruptly mid-acute gout attack without anti-inflammatory cover, encourage >= 2 L water daily, watch rash (SJS alert).

terms.simpleDefinition: Partial or complete loss of scalp or body hair secondary to chemotherapy, alopecia areata, malnutrition, or fungal tinea.
terms.definition: Partial or complete loss of scalp or body hair secondary to chemotherapy, alopecia areata, malnutrition, or fungal tinea.
terms.clinicalContext: Provide empathetic psychosocial support, scalp protection from sun/cold, and inspect scalp for tinea capitis.

terms.simpleDefinition: Fetal glycoprotein screened in maternal serum: elevated in open Neural Tube Defects/gastroschisis/twins; reduced in Trisomy 21.
terms.definition: Fetal glycoprotein screened in maternal serum: elevated in open Neural Tube Defects/gastroschisis/twins; reduced in Trisomy 21.
terms.clinicalContext: Confirm gestational age cleanly via ultrasound dating before interpreting maternal screening titres.

terms.simpleDefinition: Microscopic grape-like air sac at the end of respiratory bronchioles where O2 and CO2 gas exchange occurs.
terms.definition: Microscopic grape-like air sac at the end of respiratory bronchioles where O2 and CO2 gas exchange occurs.
terms.clinicalContext: Promote deep breathing, early ambulation, and incentive spirometry to prevent post-operative alveolar collapse (atelectasis).

terms.simpleDefinition: Absence of menstruation — physiological in pregnancy/lactation or pathological (primary > 16 yrs; secondary >= 3–6 months).
terms.definition: Absence of menstruation — physiological in pregnancy/lactation or pathological (primary > 16 yrs; secondary >= 3–6 months).
terms.clinicalContext: Perform urine beta-hCG pregnancy test FIRST in every reproductive-age woman presenting with secondary amenorrhoea.

terms.simpleDefinition: Potent bactericidal Gram-negative IV antibiotics carrying dose-limiting nephrotoxicity and irreversible CN VIII ototoxicity.
terms.definition: Potent bactericidal Gram-negative IV antibiotics carrying dose-limiting nephrotoxicity and irreversible CN VIII ototoxicity.
terms.clinicalContext: Check renal function (Creatinine/urine output) and tinnitus/vertigo before dosing; never co-mix in same IV syringe with Penicillins.

terms.simpleDefinition: Aminoglycosides & Tetracyclines reviews medicines used to treat infection or abnormal cell growth. Nursing care must balance therapeutic effect, resistance prevention, toxicity monitoring and patient adherence.
terms.definition: Aminoglycosides & Tetracyclines reviews medicines used to treat infection or abnormal cell growth. Nursing care must balance therapeutic effect, resistance prevention, toxicity monitoring and patient adherence. (Pharmacology I curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Aminoglycosides & Tetracyclines reviews medicines used to treat infection or abnormal cell growth. Nursing care must balance therapeutic effect, resistance prevention, toxicity monitoring and patient adherence.

terms.simpleDefinition: Ultrasound-guided needle aspiration of amniotic fluid for genetic, lung-maturity, or infection testing.
terms.definition: Ultrasound-guided needle aspiration of amniotic fluid for genetic, lung-maturity, or infection testing.
terms.clinicalContext: Monitor fetal heart rate, maternal vitals, and counsel Rh-negative mothers on Anti-D immunoglobulin prophylaxis.

terms.simpleDefinition: Rare catastrophic anaphylactoid reaction during/after delivery -> sudden severe hypoxia, hypotension, cardiovascular collapse, and rapid DIC bleeding.
terms.definition: Rare catastrophic anaphylactoid reaction during/after delivery -> sudden severe hypoxia, hypotension, cardiovascular collapse, and rapid DIC bleeding.
terms.clinicalContext: Summon full multidisciplinary ICU/obstetric team immediately: airway intubation, CPR/BP support, and massive transfusion for DIC.

terms.simpleDefinition: Artificial rupture of the chorioamniotic membranes using an AmniHook during active labour.
terms.definition: Artificial rupture of the chorioamniotic membranes using an AmniHook during active labour.
terms.clinicalContext: Check fetal heart rate IMMEDIATELY before and after rupture to detect umbilical cord prolapse and note liquor colour (meconium staining).

terms.simpleDefinition: Broad antifungal used in severe cryptococcal meningitis causing infusion rigors, nephrotoxicity, and severe K+/Mg2+ wasting.
terms.definition: Broad antifungal used in severe cryptococcal meningitis causing infusion rigors, nephrotoxicity, and severe K+/Mg2+ wasting.
terms.clinicalContext: Pre-hydrate with 1 L Normal Saline + KCl/MgSO4 supplementation per Uganda HIV/Cryptococcal protocol and protect IV solution per product instructions.

terms.simpleDefinition: Pancreatic digestive enzymes sharply elevated in blood during acute pancreatitis.
terms.definition: Pancreatic digestive enzymes sharply elevated in blood during acute pancreatitis.
terms.clinicalContext: Keep NBM initially in acute pancreatitis, infuse aggressive IV fluids, give opioid analgesia (avoiding hypotension), and monitor serum calcium.

terms.simpleDefinition: Anaemia is a medical nursing topic linked to oxygen transport, immunity, bleeding control, fatigue and safe preparation for procedures or referral.
terms.definition: Anaemia is a medical nursing topic linked to oxygen transport, immunity, bleeding control, fatigue and safe preparation for procedures or referral. (Medical Nursing (I) and Pharmacology (I) curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Assess pallor, fatigue, dizziness, breathlessness, fever, bleeding, bruising, lymph node enlargement and infection signs.

terms.simpleDefinition: A medicine used to relieve pain.
terms.definition: Analgesics reduce pain through different mechanisms. Examples include paracetamol, non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medicines and opioids.
terms.clinicalContext: Nurses assess pain before and after administration, check allergies, watch adverse effects and document response.
terms.example: In practice, nurses use the term analgesic when assessing, documenting or explaining patient care.
terms.mnemonics: Connect the word to assessment, documentation and safe nursing action.

terms.simpleDefinition: Three-step pain escalation: Step 1 Non-opioids (Paracetamol/NSAIDs) -> Step 2 Weak opioids (Tramadol/Codeine) -> Step 3 Strong opioids (Morphine).
terms.definition: Three-step pain escalation: Step 1 Non-opioids (Paracetamol/NSAIDs) -> Step 2 Weak opioids (Tramadol/Codeine) -> Step 3 Strong opioids (Morphine).
terms.clinicalContext: Give cancer/palliative pain analgesia strictly 'by the clock' rather than forcing patients to wait in agony 'PRN'.

terms.simpleDefinition: Rapid, life-threatening systemic allergic reaction causing airway swelling and severe hypotension.
terms.definition: Type I IgE-mediated hypersensitivity reaction triggering massive mast cell degranulation, bronchospasm, laryngeal oedema, urticaria, and distributive shock.
terms.clinicalContext: IMMEDIATE FIRST-LINE: Adrenaline (Epinephrine) 1:1000 — 0.5 mg (0.5 mL) IM into anterolateral thigh (paediatric 0.01 mg/kg), lay patient flat with legs elevated, high-flow oxygen, and IV Normal Saline.
terms.mnemonics: ABCDE + Adrenaline IM Outer Thigh FIRST (never wait for antihistamine).

terms.simpleDefinition: Extreme generalized body-wide subcutaneous oedema seen in severe nephrotic syndrome, kwashiorkor, or liver failure.
terms.definition: Extreme generalized body-wide subcutaneous oedema seen in severe nephrotic syndrome, kwashiorkor, or liver failure.
terms.clinicalContext: Handle oedematous fragile skin gently, reposition q2h, chart daily weights, and restrict sodium/fluids as ordered.

terms.simpleDefinition: Anatomy is the scientific study of the structural organization of the human body, ranging from microscopic cells to large, visible structures like organs and
terms.definition: Anatomy is the scientific study of the structural organization of the human body, ranging from microscopic cells to large, visible structures like organs and (Anatomy curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Use Introduction to Anatomy as a practical nursing topic, not only a memorized definition. Start with normal structure and function, then connect it to assessment findings and disease.

terms.term: Anatomy and Physiology of the Lymphatic System
terms.simpleDefinition: Anatomy and Physiology of Lymphatic System
terms.definition: Anatomy and Physiology of Lymphatic System (Medical Nursing (III) curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Use Anatomy and Physiology of the Lymphatic System as a practical nursing topic, not only a memorized definition. Start with normal structure and function, then connect it to assessment findings and disease.

terms.term: Anatomy and Physiology of the Musculo-skeletal System
terms.simpleDefinition: Anatomy and Physiology of the Musculoskeletal System
terms.definition: Anatomy and Physiology of the Musculoskeletal System (Medical Nursing (III) curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: The skeletal system is best revised as a living support, protection, movement, blood-forming and mineral-storage system. A nurse uses it to understand pain, deformity, movement limits, neurovascular risk and safe.

terms.term: Anatomy and Physiology of the Renal System
terms.simpleDefinition: The urinary system is the main excretory system eliminating waste products from blood through urine. Its anatomy consists of two kidneys, each joined to the
terms.definition: The urinary system is the main excretory system eliminating waste products from blood through urine. Its anatomy consists of two kidneys, each joined to the (Anatomy & physiology II curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Use The Urinary System as a practical nursing topic, not only a memorized definition. Start with normal structure and function, then connect it to assessment findings and disease.

terms.simpleDefinition: Androgens explained for mental-health nursing with medicine-safety checks, risk monitoring, adherence teaching and legal documentation priorities.
terms.definition: Androgens explained for mental-health nursing with medicine-safety checks, risk monitoring, adherence teaching and legal documentation priorities. (Mental Health Nursing(II) Pharmacology (III) curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Androgens connects medicine action to a specific body system. The nurse should review normal physiology first, then ask how each medicine changes that system and which observations prove benefit or harm.

terms.simpleDefinition: Abnormal localized ballooning of a weakened arterial wall (e.g. abdominal aorta or cerebral berry aneurysm).
terms.definition: Abnormal localized ballooning of a weakened arterial wall (e.g. abdominal aorta or cerebral berry aneurysm).
terms.clinicalContext: Control hypertension gently and NEVER deeply palpate a pulsatile abdominal mass (risk of catastrophic rupture).

terms.simpleDefinition: Anger is the strong emotion that one feels when he/she thinks that someone has behaved in an unfair, cruel or unacceptable way.
terms.definition: Anger is the strong emotion that one feels when he/she thinks that someone has behaved in an unfair, cruel or unacceptable way. (Palliative Care Nursing curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Use Anger as a practical nursing topic, not only a memorized definition. Focus on comfort, dignity, symptom control, communication and family support.

terms.simpleDefinition: Crushing/tight substernal chest pain triggered by transient myocardial ischaemia without tissue necrosis.
terms.definition: Crushing/tight substernal chest pain triggered by transient myocardial ischaemia without tissue necrosis.
terms.clinicalContext: Rest patient upright, give sublingual Glyceryl Trinitrate (GTN) q5m x 3 max checking BP >= 90 mmHg first; escalate immediately if unrelieved (possible MI).

terms.simpleDefinition: Rapid bradykinin-mediated swelling of lips, tongue, and glottis triggered unpredictably days or years after starting Enalapril/Lisinopril.
terms.definition: Rapid bradykinin-mediated swelling of lips, tongue, and glottis triggered unpredictably days or years after starting Enalapril/Lisinopril.
terms.clinicalContext: STOP ACE inhibitor permanently, protect airway urgently (unlike histamine anaphylaxis, steroids/antihistamines work poorly — prepare airway intubation!).

terms.simpleDefinition: Serum Na+ minus (Cl- + HCO3-), normal ~8–12 mEq/L; widened in DKA, Lactate shock, Uraemia, Salicylate/Methanol poisoning ('MUDPILES').
terms.definition: Serum Na+ minus (Cl- + HCO3-), normal ~8–12 mEq/L; widened in DKA, Lactate shock, Uraemia, Salicylate/Methanol poisoning ('MUDPILES').
terms.clinicalContext: Investigate unexplained high anion gap for hidden tissue sepsis hypoperfusion or toxic ingestion.

terms.simpleDefinition: Abnormal stiffening and fusion of a joint from chronic arthritis (RA/AS), trauma, or prolonged immobility.
terms.definition: Abnormal stiffening and fusion of a joint from chronic arthritis (RA/AS), trauma, or prolonged immobility.
terms.clinicalContext: Maintain functional joint alignment and perform prescribed range-of-motion physiotherapy early.

terms.simpleDefinition: Anorexia is simple loss of appetite; anorexia nervosa is a psychiatric eating disorder with intense fear of weight gain and extreme restriction.
terms.definition: Anorexia is simple loss of appetite; anorexia nervosa is a psychiatric eating disorder with intense fear of weight gain and extreme restriction.
terms.clinicalContext: Monitor electrolytes (refeeding hypophosphataemia/hypokalaemia), bradycardia, and orthostatic hypotension.

terms.simpleDefinition: Partial or total loss of smell sensation (Cranial Nerve I) following viral URTI, ethmoid fracture, or anterior fossa lesions.
terms.definition: Partial or total loss of smell sensation (Cranial Nerve I) following viral URTI, ethmoid fracture, or anterior fossa lesions.
terms.clinicalContext: Educate home safety: fit smoke detectors & check food expiry dates since spoiled food/gas leaks cannot be smelled.

terms.definition: Stroking lateral sole -> upgoing great toe extension + fanning toes: NORMAL in infants < 18–24 months; abnormal upper motor neuron corticospinal sign in adults.
terms.clinicalContext: Test routinely during focal stroke, spinal cord, or post-ictal neuro exams.

terms.simpleDefinition: A comprehensive overview of the Bachelor of Nursing Science (BNS) program, covering foundational sciences, core nursing skills, and advanced clinical
terms.definition: A comprehensive overview of the Bachelor of Nursing Science (BNS) program, covering foundational sciences, core nursing skills, and advanced clinical (Professional Nursing Issues curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Use BNS 124: Professional Nursing Issues as a practical nursing topic, not only a memorized definition. Translate theory into safe decisions, accountability, communication and service improvement.

terms.simpleDefinition: Bacteraemia is bacteria transiently in blood; Sepsis is life-threatening organ dysfunction from dysregulated host response to infection.
terms.definition: Bacteraemia is bacteria transiently in blood; Sepsis is life-threatening organ dysfunction from dysregulated host response to infection.
terms.clinicalContext: Apply 'Sepsis Six' within 1 hour: O2, blood cultures, IV antibiotics, IV fluids, lactate, and strict urine output.

terms.simpleDefinition: Polymicrobial anaerobic vaginal flora shift replacing protective Lactobacilli -> thin grey-white 'fishy' amine discharge.
terms.definition: Polymicrobial anaerobic vaginal flora shift replacing protective Lactobacilli -> thin grey-white 'fishy' amine discharge.
terms.clinicalContext: Treat symptomatic & pregnant mothers with oral Metronidazole per UCG to cut preterm birth/PROM risks cleanly.

terms.simpleDefinition: Inflammation/infection of glans penis often linked to poor hygiene under foreskin, Candida, or undiagnosed Diabetes Mellitus.
terms.definition: Inflammation/infection of glans penis often linked to poor hygiene under foreskin, Candida, or undiagnosed Diabetes Mellitus.
terms.clinicalContext: Screen fasting blood glucose in recurrent fungal balanitis and instruct gentle warm retraction/drying hygiene.

terms.simpleDefinition: Stretch pressure sensors in carotid sinus & aortic arch that rapidly modulate heart rate and vascular tone.
terms.definition: Stretch pressure sensors in carotid sinus & aortic arch that rapidly modulate heart rate and vascular tone.
terms.clinicalContext: Explain postural orthostatic dizziness to elderly patients and advise sitting on bed edge before standing.

terms.simpleDefinition: Blocked lubricated posterior labial vestibular gland causing unilateral tender swelling at 4 or 8 o'clock vulvar position.
terms.definition: Blocked lubricated posterior labial vestibular gland causing unilateral tender swelling at 4 or 8 o'clock vulvar position.
terms.clinicalContext: Provide warm sitz baths for mild cysts; warm painful abscesses require surgical marsupialization/Word catheter + STI screen.

terms.simpleDefinition: Minimal baseline energy expenditure sustaining cellular respiration, heartbeat, breathing, and core warmth at complete rest.
terms.definition: Minimal baseline energy expenditure sustaining cellular respiration, heartbeat, breathing, and core warmth at complete rest.
terms.clinicalContext: Fever raises BMR ~13% per 1 C above normal, accelerating protein catabolism and calorie needs in ICU/burn/TB wards.

terms.simpleDefinition: Basic Principles of Drug Action explains how a medicine produces its effect at receptors, enzymes, ion channels or other body targets. Nursing care links the expected action to measurable patient outcomes and early.
terms.definition: Basic Principles of Drug Action explains how a medicine produces its effect at receptors, enzymes, ion channels or other body targets. Nursing care links the expected action to measurable patient outcomes and early. (Pharmacology I curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Basic Principles of Drug Action explains how a medicine produces its effect at receptors, enzymes, ion channels or other body targets. Nursing care links the expected action to measurable patient outcomes and early.

terms.simpleDefinition: BED BATH Is bathing of a patient who is confined to bed and cannot or has no capability of self bathing.
terms.definition: BED BATH Is bathing of a patient who is confined to bed and cannot or has no capability of self bathing. (Foundations of Nursing 1 & Basic computer Anatomy curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Use Bed bath as a practical nursing topic, not only a memorized definition. Translate theory into safe decisions, accountability, communication and service improvement.

terms.simpleDefinition: BED MAKING Bed making is a key nursing skill that is essential for the promotion of patient care, comfort, hygiene and wellbeing.
terms.definition: BED MAKING Bed making is a key nursing skill that is essential for the promotion of patient care, comfort, hygiene and wellbeing. (Foundations of Nursing 1 & Basic computer Anatomy curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Use Bed making as a practical nursing topic, not only a memorized definition. Translate theory into safe decisions, accountability, communication and service improvement.

terms.simpleDefinition: Acute idiopathic lower motor neuron facial nerve paralysis affecting BOTH forehead & lower face equally (distinguishes cleanly from stroke where forehead is spared!).
terms.definition: Acute idiopathic lower motor neuron facial nerve paralysis affecting BOTH forehead & lower face equally (distinguishes cleanly from stroke where forehead is spared!).
terms.clinicalContext: Start early oral Prednisolone within 72 hours AND tape eyelid shut/apply lubricating ointment every night so exposed cornea doesn't ulcerate!

terms.simpleDefinition: Bell's palsy is a type of facial paralysis that results in a temporary inability to control the facial muscles on the affected side of the face due to
terms.definition: Bell's palsy is a type of facial paralysis that results in a temporary inability to control the facial muscles on the affected side of the face due to (Medical Nursing (III) curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Malnutrition : Difficulty in eating and drinking due to facial muscle weakness can lead to malnutrition.

terms.simpleDefinition: Brief episodic spinning vertigo (< 60 s) triggered by rolling in bed or tilting head upward due to displaced inner-ear otoliths.
terms.definition: Brief episodic spinning vertigo (< 60 s) triggered by rolling in bed or tilting head upward due to displaced inner-ear otoliths.
terms.clinicalContext: Assist patient slowly up from lying, protect from falls, and coordinate Epley canalith repositioning.

terms.simpleDefinition: Non-malignant enlargement of periurethral prostate causing weak stream, hesitancy, nocturia, and acute urinary retention.
terms.definition: Non-malignant enlargement of periurethral prostate causing weak stream, hesitancy, nocturia, and acute urinary retention.
terms.clinicalContext: Insert Coude/Foley catheter carefully per protocol; never abruptly clamp/drain > 1,000 mL if haematuria/post-obstructive diuresis risk.

terms.simpleDefinition: Bereavement is the state of having lost something or someone.
terms.definition: Bereavement is the state of having lost something or someone. (Paediatric Nursing (i) curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Chronic Depression: Prolonged and persistent feelings of sadness, hopelessness, and lack of interest in previously enjoyed activities.

terms.simpleDefinition: Cardio-protective drugs (Atenolol, Propranolol, Carvedilol) slowing HR and contractility via beta-receptor blockade.
terms.definition: Cardio-protective drugs (Atenolol, Propranolol, Carvedilol) slowing HR and contractility via beta-receptor blockade.
terms.clinicalContext: Check apical HR >= 60 bpm & SBP before dose; avoid non-selective Propranolol in asthmatics (bronchospasm) and warn diabetics it masks hypoglycaemia tachycardia.

terms.simpleDefinition: Primary extracellular blood acid-base chemical buffer balancing CO2 + H2O <-> H2CO3 <-> H+ + HCO3- within seconds.
terms.definition: Primary extracellular blood acid-base chemical buffer balancing CO2 + H2O <-> H2CO3 <-> H+ + HCO3- within seconds.
terms.clinicalContext: Remember lungs blow off volatile CO2 quickly while kidneys excrete fixed H+ & regenerate bicarbonate over days.

terms.simpleDefinition: Yellow haemoglobin breakdown pigment; unconjugated levels crossing newborn blood-brain barrier stain basal ganglia (kernicterus).
terms.definition: Yellow haemoglobin breakdown pigment; unconjugated levels crossing newborn blood-brain barrier stain basal ganglia (kernicterus).
terms.clinicalContext: Initiate intensive blue-light phototherapy early with opaque eye shields, frequent feeds, and hydration.

terms.simpleDefinition: Tissue sampling submitted in 10% neutral buffered formalin (NEVER freeze histology specimen!) for definitive histological diagnosis.
terms.definition: Tissue sampling submitted in 10% neutral buffered formalin (NEVER freeze histology specimen!) for definitive histological diagnosis.
terms.clinicalContext: Verify correct patient labelling, intact fixative seal, bleeding check post-procedure, and timely pathology tracking.

terms.simpleDefinition: Bipolar Affective Disorder is studied through child and adolescent mental-health nursing because symptoms affect development, school, family relationships, safety and long-term functioning.
terms.definition: Bipolar Affective Disorder is studied through child and adolescent mental-health nursing because symptoms affect development, school, family relationships, safety and long-term functioning. (Mental Health Nursing(II) Pharmacology (III) curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Bipolar Affective Disorder is studied through child and adolescent mental-health nursing because symptoms affect development, school, family relationships, safety and long-term functioning.

terms.simpleDefinition: 0–13 cervical readiness grading scale (dilation, effacement, station, consistency, position) before labour induction.
terms.definition: 0–13 cervical readiness grading scale (dilation, effacement, station, consistency, position) before labour induction.
terms.clinicalContext: Score <= 5 signals unfavourable cervix needing prostaglandin (Misoprostol) ripening before Oxytocin.

terms.simpleDefinition: Severe malaria complication featuring massive intravascular haemolysis and dark Coca-Cola-coloured haemoglobinuria.
terms.definition: Severe malaria complication featuring massive intravascular haemolysis and dark Coca-Cola-coloured haemoglobinuria.
terms.clinicalContext: Monitor urine output urgently, check renal function & Hb for packed RBC transfusion, and monitor on IV Artesunate.

terms.simpleDefinition: Non-invasive bedside ultrasound calculating residual urine volume without risking catheter CAUTI.
terms.definition: Non-invasive bedside ultrasound calculating residual urine volume without risking catheter CAUTI.
terms.clinicalContext: PVR < 50–100 mL normal; >= 300–400 mL post-void signals urinary retention needing intermittent/indwelling catheter assessment.

terms.simpleDefinition: Chronic flaky crusting inflammation along eyelid margins from seborrhoea or Staph infection causing gritty morning lashes.
terms.definition: Chronic flaky crusting inflammation along eyelid margins from seborrhoea or Staph infection causing gritty morning lashes.
terms.clinicalContext: Demonstrate gentle warm eyelid compresses followed by diluted baby-shampoo lid scrubs + clean margin wiping.

terms.simpleDefinition: Blood is a vital connective tissue that circulates throughout the body, acting as a transport system and playing roles in defense and maintaining balance.
terms.definition: Blood is a vital connective tissue that circulates throughout the body, acting as a transport system and playing roles in defense and maintaining balance. (Anatomy & physiology 1 & First aid curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Use Blood and its composition as a practical nursing topic, not only a memorized definition. Prioritize airway, breathing, circulation, pain, asepsis, wound healing and early complication detection.

terms.simpleDefinition: The amount of sugar in the blood.
terms.definition: Blood glucose is a key energy measurement. It can become too high or too low in diabetes, illness, fasting or medication effects.
terms.clinicalContext: Nurses monitor glucose, recognize hypoglycaemia or hyperglycaemia signs and follow facility protocols.
terms.example: In practice, nurses use the term blood glucose when assessing, documenting or explaining patient care.
terms.mnemonics: Connect the word to assessment, documentation and safe nursing action.

terms.simpleDefinition: The force of blood pushing against artery walls.
terms.definition: Blood pressure is recorded as systolic pressure over diastolic pressure. It reflects circulation, vascular resistance and heart pumping action.
terms.clinicalContext: Nurses measure blood pressure accurately, compare it with baseline and report very high, very low or rapidly changing readings.
terms.example: In practice, nurses use the term blood pressure when assessing, documenting or explaining patient care.
terms.mnemonics: Connect the word to assessment, documentation and safe nursing action.

terms.simpleDefinition: Blood transfusion refers to the intravenous replacement of lost or destroyed blood with compatible human blood.
terms.definition: Blood transfusion refers to the intravenous replacement of lost or destroyed blood with compatible human blood. (Surgical Nursing (I) and Gynecological Nursing curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: The following are some of the adverse reactions which may occur during blood transfusion:

terms.simpleDefinition: Immune or infectious reaction (febrile, acute haemolytic ABO mismatch, urticarial, TRALI) during blood infusion.
terms.definition: Immune or infectious reaction (febrile, acute haemolytic ABO mismatch, urticarial, TRALI) during blood infusion.
terms.clinicalContext: If acute fever, chills, flank pain, or hypotension occurs: STOP TRANSFUSION IMMEDIATELY, keep vein open with fresh 0.9% NaCl tubing, check patient/bag ID, notify blood bank.

terms.simpleDefinition: Tight endothelial astrocyte junction shielding brain CSF from circulating toxins, microbes, and water-soluble drugs.
terms.definition: Tight endothelial astrocyte junction shielding brain CSF from circulating toxins, microbes, and water-soluble drugs.
terms.clinicalContext: Lipid-soluble drugs (Diazepam, Propofol) cross instantaneously; water-soluble Penicillins require inflamed meninges or high IV dosing.

terms.simpleDefinition: Explore the detailed topics covered in Anatomy & Physiology.
terms.definition: Explore the detailed topics covered in Anatomy & Physiology. (Anatomy curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Use Histology Introduction as a practical nursing topic, not only a memorized definition. Start with normal structure and function, then connect it to assessment findings and disease.

terms.simpleDefinition: Explore the detailed topics covered in Foundations of Nursing.
terms.definition: Explore the detailed topics covered in Foundations of Nursing. (Foundations of Nursing curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: An introduction to the core concepts, theories, and philosophies that define professional nursing practice, from its historical evolution to the application of the nursing process.

terms.simpleDefinition: Explore the complete Physiology curriculum from Year I to Year II.
terms.definition: Explore the complete Physiology curriculum from Year I to Year II. (Physiology curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Use Cell Function & Transport as a practical nursing topic, not only a memorized definition. Start with normal structure and function, then connect it to assessment findings and disease.

terms.simpleDefinition: Explore the detailed topics covered in Health Assessment.
terms.definition: Explore the detailed topics covered in Health Assessment. (Health Assessment curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: A comprehensive guide to patient assessment, covering interviewing skills, physical examination techniques, mental status evaluation, and the interpretation of laboratory and diagnostic studies.

terms.simpleDefinition: Explore the detailed topics covered in Computer Skills.
terms.definition: Explore the detailed topics covered in Computer Skills. (Computer Skills curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Assess ABCDE & vital trends systematically, identify early red-flag deterioration, document clearly, and initiate priority nursing interventions.

terms.simpleDefinition: Explore the detailed topics covered in Nursing Informatics.
terms.definition: Explore the detailed topics covered in Nursing Informatics. (Nursing Informatics curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: An introduction to the use of information and technology in healthcare, focusing on electronic health records, telehealth, and the ethical considerations for nurses.

terms.simpleDefinition: An introduction to the basic principles of drug action, covering pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, and the pharmacology of major drug classes.
terms.definition: An introduction to the basic principles of drug action, covering pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, and the pharmacology of major drug classes. (Professional Nursing Issues curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Use BNS 121: Pharmacology I as a practical nursing topic, not only a memorized definition. Study medicines through indication, safety checks, expected response, adverse effects and patient teaching.

terms.simpleDefinition: Explore the detailed topics covered in Microbiology.
terms.definition: Explore the detailed topics covered in Microbiology. (Microbiology curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Use Sterilization & Disinfection as a practical nursing topic, not only a memorized definition. Link cause, transmission, incubation, clinical features, treatment support and prevention.

terms.simpleDefinition: An introduction to the fundamental basis of pathological processes, from cell injury and inflammation to the systemic effects of disease.
terms.definition: An introduction to the fundamental basis of pathological processes, from cell injury and inflammation to the systemic effects of disease. (Pathology curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Use Concepts & Application as a practical nursing topic, not only a memorized definition. Start with normal structure and function, then connect it to assessment findings and disease.

terms.simpleDefinition: Explore the complete Biochemistry curriculum from Year I to Year II.
terms.definition: Explore the complete Biochemistry curriculum from Year I to Year II. (Biochemistry curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Use Chemistry Refresh (Atoms) as a practical nursing topic, not only a memorized definition. Start with normal structure and function, then connect it to assessment findings and disease.

terms.simpleDefinition: Weight in kg divided by height in metres squared (Normal 18.5–24.9 kg/m2; Obesity >= 30).
terms.definition: Weight in kg divided by height in metres squared (Normal 18.5–24.9 kg/m2; Obesity >= 30).
terms.clinicalContext: In under-5s and pregnant mothers, use MUAC (< 11.5 cm SAM / < 23 cm maternal undernutrition) rather than adult BMI.

terms.simpleDefinition: Mosteller square-root formula calculating individualized chemotherapy and paediatric high-precision doses (m2).
terms.definition: Mosteller square-root formula calculating individualized chemotherapy and paediatric high-precision doses (m2).
terms.clinicalContext: Always verify weight (kg) AND height (cm) cleanly before checking double-verified chemotherapy charts.

terms.simpleDefinition: Sterile extraction of marrow from posterior iliac crest (or sternum) diagnosing leukaemia, aplastic anaemia, or visceral leishmaniasis.
terms.definition: Sterile extraction of marrow from posterior iliac crest (or sternum) diagnosing leukaemia, aplastic anaemia, or visceral leishmaniasis.
terms.clinicalContext: Apply firm sterile pressure dressing 10–15 min post-procedure and watch closely for haematoma or infection.

terms.simpleDefinition: Spirochaete infection (Ornithodoros soft tick in mud-walled dwellings) causing recurring high fever episodes, hepatosplenomegaly, and pregnancy loss.
terms.definition: Spirochaete infection (Ornithodoros soft tick in mud-walled dwellings) causing recurring high fever episodes, hepatosplenomegaly, and pregnancy loss.
terms.clinicalContext: Give Penicillin/Doxycycline cautiously — monitor patient FIRST 2–4 hours closely for acute Jarisch-Herxheimer fever/hypotension crisis.

terms.simpleDefinition: Mechanical or paralytic blockage of intestinal transit causing colicky pain, bilious/faeculent vomiting, and obstipation.
terms.definition: Mechanical or paralytic blockage of intestinal transit causing colicky pain, bilious/faeculent vomiting, and obstipation.
terms.clinicalContext: Place patient NBM, insert NGT for low intermittent suction, infuse IV fluids + K+ replacement, and prep for surgery if strangulation suspected.

terms.simpleDefinition: BPH Drugs explained for mental-health nursing with medicine-safety checks, risk monitoring, adherence teaching and legal documentation priorities.
terms.definition: BPH Drugs explained for mental-health nursing with medicine-safety checks, risk monitoring, adherence teaching and legal documentation priorities. (Mental Health Nursing(II) Pharmacology (III) curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: BPH Drugs connects medicine action to a specific body system. The nurse should review normal physiology first, then ask how each medicine changes that system and which observations prove benefit or harm.

terms.simpleDefinition: Excessive lateral traction during shoulder dystocia stretching C5–C6 nerve roots -> infant arm adducted, internally rotated ('waiter's tip' position).
terms.definition: Excessive lateral traction during shoulder dystocia stretching C5–C6 nerve roots -> infant arm adducted, internally rotated ('waiter's tip' position).
terms.clinicalContext: Perform gentle passive ROM after initial swelling settles (~Day 7–10), reassure parents on frequent recovery, avoid forceful shoulder pull during birth.

terms.simpleDefinition: Abnormally slow resting heart rate below 60 beats per minute in adults.
terms.definition: Can result from vagal stimulation, beta-blocker or digoxin toxicity, hypothyroidism, inferior MI, sick sinus syndrome, or increased intracranial pressure (Cushing's reflex).
terms.clinicalContext: Always hold digoxin or beta-blockers if adult HR < 60 bpm per facility protocol and assess blood pressure, dizziness, or syncope urgently.

terms.simpleDefinition: Slowness initiating & executing voluntary movements characteristic of Parkinson's disease nigrostriatal dopamine loss.
terms.definition: Slowness initiating & executing voluntary movements characteristic of Parkinson's disease nigrostriatal dopamine loss.
terms.clinicalContext: Allow unhurried time for walking/dressing, give visual step cues, and time Levodopa/Carbidopa doses on time every day.

terms.simpleDefinition: Irregular painless uterine tightening from 2nd trimester causing ZERO progressive cervical dilation ('false labour').
terms.definition: Irregular painless uterine tightening from 2nd trimester causing ZERO progressive cervical dilation ('false labour').
terms.clinicalContext: Differentiate cleanly from true labour (regular intensifying interval + cervical effacement/dilation) by hydration, walking rest check, and palpation.

terms.simpleDefinition: Breaking bad news to patients and their families is one of the most difficult responsibilities in health care.
terms.definition: Breaking bad news to patients and their families is one of the most difficult responsibilities in health care. (Palliative Care Nursing curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Use Breaking sad news as a practical nursing topic, not only a memorized definition. Focus on comfort, dignity, symptom control, communication and family support.

terms.simpleDefinition: Fetal buttocks or feet enter pelvic brim first (~3–4% at term); Footling breech carries highest umbilical cord prolapse risk.
terms.definition: Fetal buttocks or feet enter pelvic brim first (~3–4% at term); Footling breech carries highest umbilical cord prolapse risk.
terms.clinicalContext: Confirm via Leopold abdominal palpation & ultrasound after 36 weeks; refer early for External Cephalic Version (ECV) or safe CEmONC hospital delivery.

terms.simpleDefinition: Permanent abnormal bronchial dilation with chronic foul copious three-layered sputum, coarse crackles, and finger clubbing.
terms.definition: Permanent abnormal bronchial dilation with chronic foul copious three-layered sputum, coarse crackles, and finger clubbing.
terms.clinicalContext: Provide daily postural percussion drainage, hydration, sputum cultures for exacerbations, and vaccinations.

terms.simpleDefinition: Acute viral lower airway inflammation in infants < 2 years causing wheezing, nasal flaring, subcostal indrawing, and poor feeding.
terms.definition: Acute viral lower airway inflammation in infants < 2 years causing wheezing, nasal flaring, subcostal indrawing, and poor feeding.
terms.clinicalContext: Provide gentle nasal suction before feeds, humidified O2 if SpO2 < 90–92%, and small frequent NGT/IV fluids; routine antibiotics/steroids rarely help viral bronchiolitis.

terms.simpleDefinition: Bronchitis is a respiratory nursing topic because it can interfere with airway patency, breathing effort, oxygen exchange, infection control and safe activity.
terms.definition: Bronchitis is a respiratory nursing topic because it can interfere with airway patency, breathing effort, oxygen exchange, infection control and safe activity. (Medical Nursing (I) and Pharmacology (I) curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Assess respiratory rate, work of breathing, oxygen saturation, temperature, pulse, chest pain and ability to speak full sentences.

terms.simpleDefinition: Bronchopulmonary Dysplasia (BPD)
terms.definition: Bronchopulmonary Dysplasia (BPD) (Surgical Nursing III and Paediatric Nursing (II) curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Use Broncho pulmonary dysplasia/ chronic lung disease as a practical nursing topic, not only a memorized definition. Prioritize airway, breathing, circulation, pain, asepsis, wound healing and early complication.

terms.simpleDefinition: Medication that relaxes bronchial smooth muscle to open constricted airways.
terms.definition: Includes short-acting beta-2 agonists (Salbutamol), anticholinergics (Ipratropium), and methylxanthines (Aminophylline) used in asthma and COPD exacerbations.
terms.clinicalContext: Deliver short-acting Salbutamol FIRST before inhaled corticosteroids so bronchodilation opens airways cleanly; monitor heart rate for tachycardia and tremors.

terms.simpleDefinition: Brucellosis is studied as a tropical or communicable-disease nursing topic because it can affect the patient, household and community. Nursing care connects early recognition, isolation or prevention measures,.
terms.definition: Brucellosis is studied as a tropical or communicable-disease nursing topic because it can affect the patient, household and community. Nursing care connects early recognition, isolation or prevention measures,. (Medical Nursing (II) and Tropical Medicines curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Assess fever, rash, cough, diarrhoea, vomiting, bleeding, dehydration, pain, mental state, nutritional status and exposure history.

terms.simpleDefinition: Brucellosis is a zoonotic bacterial infection of acute onset, commonly known as undulant fever, Malta fever, or abortus fever.
terms.definition: Brucellosis is a zoonotic bacterial infection of acute onset, commonly known as undulant fever, Malta fever, or abortus fever. (Midwifery II & Tropical medicine curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Adults and children > 8 years:

terms.simpleDefinition: Classic meningeal irritation reflexes where passive neck flexion flexes hips/knees (Brudzinski) or knee extension causes hamstring pain (Kernig).
terms.definition: Classic meningeal irritation reflexes where passive neck flexion flexes hips/knees (Brudzinski) or knee extension causes hamstring pain (Kernig).
terms.clinicalContext: Recognize neck stiffness + photophobia + fever as acute Meningitis urgency requiring lumbar puncture & IV Ceftriaxone cleanly.

terms.simpleDefinition: Temporary non-invasive leg foam-boot traction stabilizing hip/femoral fractures pre-operatively to relieve painful muscle spasms.
terms.definition: Temporary non-invasive leg foam-boot traction stabilizing hip/femoral fractures pre-operatively to relieve painful muscle spasms.
terms.clinicalContext: Inspect heels/peroneal nerve pressure daily, ensure weights hang FREELY off the floor at all times, and NEVER lift traction weights arbitrarily.

terms.simpleDefinition: Estimates TBSA burned (Head 9%, Arms 9% each, Anterior/Posterior trunk 18% each, Legs 18% each, Perineum 1%).
terms.definition: Estimates TBSA burned (Head 9%, Arms 9% each, Anterior/Posterior trunk 18% each, Legs 18% each, Perineum 1%).
terms.clinicalContext: Parkland formula for 24h Ringer's Lactate = 4 mL × kg × %TBSA — give HALF in first 8 hours from time of burn, maintaining adult urine output 30–50 mL/hr.

terms.simpleDefinition: Burns are injuries to the skin due to extremes of temperature i.e cold or hot, chemicals or radiations. Burns occur when there is injury to the tissues of the
terms.definition: Burns are injuries to the skin due to extremes of temperature i.e cold or hot, chemicals or radiations. Burns occur when there is injury to the tissues of the (Surgical Nursing (I) and Gynecological Nursing curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Disease-commonly epilepsy, leprosy

terms.simpleDefinition: Painful fluid-filled swelling of periarticular bursae (olecranon elbow, prepatellar knee) from repetitive friction or gout/sepsis.
terms.definition: Painful fluid-filled swelling of periarticular bursae (olecranon elbow, prepatellar knee) from repetitive friction or gout/sepsis.
terms.clinicalContext: Rest joint, apply ice first 24–48 hrs, aspirate ONLY under strict sterility if septic bursitis suspected.

terms.simpleDefinition: Business encompasses a wide range of activities involving the production, distribution, and exchange of goods and services for profit.
terms.definition: Business encompasses a wide range of activities involving the production, distribution, and exchange of goods and services for profit. (Health Services Management & Entrepreneurship curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Use Business or Business Enterprise as a practical nursing topic, not only a memorized definition. Translate theory into safe decisions, accountability, communication and service improvement.

terms.simpleDefinition: Business ethics are moral principles which are recognized in respect to a particular class of human actions or a particular group.
terms.definition: Business ethics are moral principles which are recognized in respect to a particular class of human actions or a particular group. (Health Services Management & Entrepreneurship curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Use Business Ethics as a practical nursing topic, not only a memorized definition. Translate theory into safe decisions, accountability, communication and service improvement.

terms.simpleDefinition: Business idea is an identified situation that can be changed into a real and profitable activity or business.
terms.definition: Business idea is an identified situation that can be changed into a real and profitable activity or business. (Health Service Management and Entrepreneurship curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Use Business opportunities as a practical nursing topic, not only a memorized definition. Translate theory into safe decisions, accountability, communication and service improvement.

terms.simpleDefinition: When one has identified a business Opportunity to execute, one is not advised to immediately execute the businesses, a thorough process of planning for how
terms.definition: When one has identified a business Opportunity to execute, one is not advised to immediately execute the businesses, a thorough process of planning for how (Health Services Management & Entrepreneurship curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Use Business planning as a practical nursing topic, not only a memorized definition. Translate theory into safe decisions, accountability, communication and service improvement.

terms.simpleDefinition: Competitive business environment
terms.definition: Competitive business environment (Health Service Management and Entrepreneurship curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Use Setting up a Business as a practical nursing topic, not only a memorized definition. Translate theory into safe decisions, accountability, communication and service improvement.

terms.simpleDefinition: Methylxanthine CNS stimulant lowering apnoea frequency & extubation failure in preterm neonates < 34 weeks.
terms.definition: Methylxanthine CNS stimulant lowering apnoea frequency & extubation failure in preterm neonates < 34 weeks.
terms.clinicalContext: Hold or review dose if neonatal resting tachycardia > 180–200 bpm or marked jitteriness/feeding intolerance develops.

terms.simpleDefinition: Vascular smooth muscle vasodilators lowering blood pressure and severe pre-eclampsia hypertension cleanly.
terms.definition: Vascular smooth muscle vasodilators lowering blood pressure and severe pre-eclampsia hypertension cleanly.
terms.clinicalContext: Advise slow rising to prevent orthostatic dizziness, avoid grapefruit juice where applicable, and report ankle oedema or gingival hyperplasia.

terms.simpleDefinition: Breast cancer occurs when cells in the breast grow and divide uncontrollably, forming a mass of tissue known as a tumour.
terms.definition: Breast cancer occurs when cells in the breast grow and divide uncontrollably, forming a mass of tissue known as a tumour. (Surgical Nursing (I) and Gynecological Nursing curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Management depends on the tumour’s location and size, lab test results, and whether the cancer has spread.

terms.simpleDefinition: Opportunistic yeast causing white removable curdy plaques on oral mucosa or thick curdy vaginal discharge.
terms.definition: Opportunistic yeast causing white removable curdy plaques on oral mucosa or thick curdy vaginal discharge.
terms.clinicalContext: Always suspect underlying HIV immunosuppression, uncontrolled diabetes, or recent steroid inhaler use without mouth rinsing.

terms.simpleDefinition: Bright beefy-red confluent groin crease rash WITH classic pinpoint 'satellite' pustules beyond border.
terms.definition: Bright beefy-red confluent groin crease rash WITH classic pinpoint 'satellite' pustules beyond border.
terms.clinicalContext: Apply topical Nystatin/Clotrimazole cream after washing gently with plain warm water + air drying (hydrocortisone alone worsens fungal rash!).

terms.simpleDefinition: A quick test of blood flow to small vessels.
terms.definition: Capillary refill is checked by pressing a nail bed or skin area and observing how quickly normal colour returns.
terms.clinicalContext: Slow refill may suggest poor perfusion, cold exposure, dehydration or shock, and should be interpreted with other observations.
terms.example: In practice, nurses use the term capillary refill when assessing, documenting or explaining patient care.
terms.mnemonics: Connect the word to assessment, documentation and safe nursing action.

terms.simpleDefinition: Seconds required for blanched nailbed or sternum capillary bed to regain pink colour (Normal <= 2 seconds).
terms.definition: Seconds required for blanched nailbed or sternum capillary bed to regain pink colour (Normal <= 2 seconds).
terms.clinicalContext: CRT >= 3 seconds indicates hypovolaemic/septic peripheral hypoperfusion or hypothermia.

terms.simpleDefinition: Caput = soft boggy scalp oedema CROSSING suture lines present at birth resolving in days. Cephalhaematoma = subperiosteal blood collection NEVER crossing suture lines rising after hours, risking hyperbilirubinaemia.
terms.definition: Caput = soft boggy scalp oedema CROSSING suture lines present at birth resolving in days. Cephalhaematoma = subperiosteal blood collection NEVER crossing suture lines rising after hours, risking hyperbilirubinaemia.
terms.clinicalContext: NEVER aspirate a cephalhaematoma (introduces osteomyelitis/meningitis!) — monitor jaundice cleanly.
