terms.simpleDefinition: Conflict is an expressed struggle between at least two interdependent parties.
terms.definition: Conflict is an expressed struggle between at least two interdependent parties. (Health service management and entrepreneurship curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Conflict management is the practice of identifying and handling a conflict in a sensible, fair and efficient manner.

terms.term: Congenital Abnormalities of the Reproductive Organs
terms.simpleDefinition: Congenital abnormalities of the female reproductive tract are developmental abnormalities in the reproductive organs that form in the embryo.
terms.definition: Congenital abnormalities of the female reproductive tract are developmental abnormalities in the reproductive organs that form in the embryo. (Gynaecology (II) and Reproductive Health (II) curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: A multidisciplinary team consisting of gynecologists, pediatricians, geneticists, psychologists, nurses, and other specialists is often involved in the management of congenital abnormalities.

terms.simpleDefinition: Congenital cataracts are a type of cataract that occurs at birth or during a baby's first year of life, characterized by clouding or opacity of the lens of
terms.definition: Congenital cataracts are a type of cataract that occurs at birth or during a baby's first year of life, characterized by clouding or opacity of the lens of (Paediatric Nursing (III) curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Management and treatment of congenital cataracts involve a multidisciplinary approach and may vary depending on the specific case and underlying cause.

terms.simpleDefinition: Structural fetal heart defects causing left-to-right overload or cyanotic right-to-left shunting ('Tet spells').
terms.definition: Structural fetal heart defects causing left-to-right overload or cyanotic right-to-left shunting ('Tet spells').
terms.clinicalContext: During an infant hypercyanotic Tet spell: IMMEDIATELY place knees-to-chest (squatting position), give high-flow O2, calm the baby, and summon emergency physician.

terms.simpleDefinition: Congestive Cardiac Failure is studied as a cardiovascular nursing problem because it affects perfusion, oxygen delivery, workload of the heart, tissue viability and the patient's ability to perform daily activities.
terms.definition: Congestive Cardiac Failure is studied as a cardiovascular nursing problem because it affects perfusion, oxygen delivery, workload of the heart, tissue viability and the patient's ability to perform daily activities. (Medical Nursing (I) and Pharmacology (I) curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Check blood pressure, pulse rate, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation, temperature, pain score and level of consciousness.

terms.simpleDefinition: Pale lower inner eyelid mucosal vasculature indicating significant clinical anaemia (Hb often < 7–9 g/dL); confirm via palmar/nailbed pallor & Hb lab check.
terms.definition: Pale lower inner eyelid mucosal vasculature indicating significant clinical anaemia (Hb often < 7–9 g/dL); confirm via palmar/nailbed pallor & Hb lab check.
terms.clinicalContext: Examine lower palpebral conjunctivae softly in bright natural daylight.

terms.simpleDefinition: Inflammation of ocular conjunctiva; ophthalmia neonatorum (< 28 days) from Gonorrhoea/Chlamydia risks rapid corneal blindness.
terms.definition: Inflammation of ocular conjunctiva; ophthalmia neonatorum (< 28 days) from Gonorrhoea/Chlamydia risks rapid corneal blindness.
terms.clinicalContext: Apply routine Tetracycline 1% eye ointment at birth; wipe discharge inner-to-outer canthus using separate sterile swabs for each eye.

terms.simpleDefinition: Tissue that supports, binds, protects and connects body parts.
terms.definition: Connective tissue includes bone, cartilage, blood, adipose tissue and loose support tissue. It gives structure and support to organs and body systems.
terms.clinicalContext: Nurses meet connective tissue concepts in wound healing, fractures, pressure injury prevention, blood disorders and mobility care.
terms.example: In practice, nurses use the term connective tissue when assessing, documenting or explaining patient care.
terms.mnemonics: Connect the word to assessment, documentation and safe nursing action.

terms.simpleDefinition: Hormonal (pills, DMPA, implants), intrauterine (Cu-IUD), barrier, and surgical methods preventing unintended pregnancy.
terms.definition: Hormonal (pills, DMPA, implants), intrauterine (Cu-IUD), barrier, and surgical methods preventing unintended pregnancy.
terms.clinicalContext: Verify UKMEC/WHO medical eligibility (e.g. avoid combined oestrogen pills in breastfeeding < 6 weeks, migraine with aura, or uncontrolled hypertension).

terms.simpleDefinition: Contraceptives explained for mental-health nursing with medicine-safety checks, risk monitoring, adherence teaching and legal documentation priorities.
terms.definition: Contraceptives explained for mental-health nursing with medicine-safety checks, risk monitoring, adherence teaching and legal documentation priorities. (Mental Health Nursing(II) Pharmacology (III) curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Contraceptives connects medicine action to a specific body system. The nurse should review normal physiology first, then ask how each medicine changes that system and which observations prove benefit or harm.

terms.simpleDefinition: Permanent fixed shortening of muscle, tendon, or scar skin pulling a joint out of functional position.
terms.definition: Permanent fixed shortening of muscle, tendon, or scar skin pulling a joint out of functional position.
terms.clinicalContext: Prevent cleanly in stroke/burn wards via neutral splinting, prone/extension positioning, and daily passive full range-of-motion.

terms.simpleDefinition: Cooperatives are often formed to provide goods or services to their members at a lower cost than they would be able to obtain from a traditional business.
terms.definition: Cooperatives are often formed to provide goods or services to their members at a lower cost than they would be able to obtain from a traditional business. (Health Services Management & Entrepreneurship curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Use Cooperatives as a practical nursing topic, not only a memorized definition. Translate theory into safe decisions, accountability, communication and service improvement.

terms.simpleDefinition: Obstetric emergency where umbilical cord descends below presenting fetal part after membrane rupture causing lethal cord compression.
terms.definition: Obstetric emergency where umbilical cord descends below presenting fetal part after membrane rupture causing lethal cord compression.
terms.clinicalContext: Keep gloved fingers in vagina continuously pushing presenting part UP off the cord, place mother in knee-chest/exaggerated Sims position, do NOT handle/push cord back, rush to Caesarean theatre.

terms.simpleDefinition: Corneal ulcers are open sores or epithelial defects with underlying inflammation on the cornea, the transparent front part of the eye that covers the iris and
terms.definition: Corneal ulcers are open sores or epithelial defects with underlying inflammation on the cornea, the transparent front part of the eye that covers the iris and (Tropical Medicine and Surgical nursing lll curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Anti-Infective Agents: Antibiotic, antiviral, or antifungal eye drops/ointments are used depending on the cause. For viral ulcers, oral antiviral medications may also be prescribed.

terms.simpleDefinition: Plaque rupture + coronary thrombus causing irreversible myocardial muscle necrosis with crushing chest pain, diaphoresis, and ST elevation.
terms.definition: Plaque rupture + coronary thrombus causing irreversible myocardial muscle necrosis with crushing chest pain, diaphoresis, and ST elevation.
terms.clinicalContext: Give MONA-style acute stabilization cleanly (Oxygen ONLY if hypoxic < 90–94%, chewed Aspirin 300 mg, GTN if BP allows, Morphine IV cautiously, urgent reperfusion/ECG).

terms.simpleDefinition: Trimethoprim-Sulfamethoxazole preventive daily tablet reducing PCP pneumonia, Toxoplasmosis, & malaria bacterial morbidity in PLHIV.
terms.definition: Trimethoprim-Sulfamethoxazole preventive daily tablet reducing PCP pneumonia, Toxoplasmosis, & malaria bacterial morbidity in PLHIV.
terms.clinicalContext: Maintain good hydration to prevent sulfonamide crystalluria and monitor immediately for itchy rash/mucosal blisters (SJS).

terms.simpleDefinition: Twelve paired brain-stem/forebrain nerves controlling smell, vision, eye movements, facial sensation/expression, hearing, swallowing, and tongue movement.
terms.definition: Twelve paired brain-stem/forebrain nerves controlling smell, vision, eye movements, facial sensation/expression, hearing, swallowing, and tongue movement.
terms.clinicalContext: Assess gag reflex (CN IX & X) rigorously BEFORE offering water post-stroke to prevent silent aspiration.

terms.simpleDefinition: Crunch-like 'Rice Krispies' crackling beneath skin (subcutaneous emphysema after pneumothorax/chest injury) OR grating bone ends in fractures.
terms.definition: Crunch-like 'Rice Krispies' crackling beneath skin (subcutaneous emphysema after pneumothorax/chest injury) OR grating bone ends in fractures.
terms.clinicalContext: Mark margin of neck/chest subcutaneous air smoothly with pen and report expanding air track immediately.

terms.simpleDefinition: Parainfluenza viral subglottic airway swelling in ages 6m–3y causing harsh seal-like 'barking' cough, hoarseness, & inspiratory stridor.
terms.definition: Parainfluenza viral subglottic airway swelling in ages 6m–3y causing harsh seal-like 'barking' cough, hoarseness, & inspiratory stridor.
terms.clinicalContext: Treat promptly with single oral/IM Dexamethasone (0.15–0.6 mg/kg) + nebulized Adrenaline if stridor persists at rest; keep child calm with parent.

terms.simpleDefinition: Opportunistic encapsulated fungal meningitis in advanced HIV (CD4 < 100) causing severe headache, raised ICP, and cranial palsies.
terms.definition: Opportunistic encapsulated fungal meningitis in advanced HIV (CD4 < 100) causing severe headache, raised ICP, and cranial palsies.
terms.clinicalContext: Verify CrAg test, monitor therapeutic lumbar puncture CSF opening pressure relief cleanly, and monitor Amphotericin B potassium/magnesium levels carefully.

terms.simpleDefinition: Periumbilical bluish bruising (Cullen) or flank ecchymosis (Grey-Turner) signaling retroperitoneal haemorrhage in severe acute pancreatitis or ruptured ectopic pregnancy.
terms.definition: Periumbilical bluish bruising (Cullen) or flank ecchymosis (Grey-Turner) signaling retroperitoneal haemorrhage in severe acute pancreatitis or ruptured ectopic pregnancy.
terms.clinicalContext: Immediately escalate hypovolaemic volume support & urgent abdominal surgical imaging.

terms.simpleDefinition: Cushing's syndrome is simply defined as a hormonal disorder associated with excessive production of corticosteroids by the adrenal gland or the pituitary
terms.definition: Cushing's syndrome is simply defined as a hormonal disorder associated with excessive production of corticosteroids by the adrenal gland or the pituitary (Medical Nursing (III) curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Assessment Nursing Diagnosis Goals/Expected Outcomes Interventions Rationale Evaluation

terms.simpleDefinition: Syndrome = chronic cortisol excess (moon face, buffalo hump, striae, hyperglycaemia). Triad = brainstem herniation red alert (widening pulse pressure/HTN, bradycardia, irregular respirations).
terms.definition: Syndrome = chronic cortisol excess (moon face, buffalo hump, striae, hyperglycaemia). Triad = brainstem herniation red alert (widening pulse pressure/HTN, bradycardia, irregular respirations).
terms.clinicalContext: Elevate head of bed 30° neutral neck alignment and summon neurosurgical help immediately for Cushing's Triad.

terms.simpleDefinition: Customer care refers to the practice that enables an organization to deliver services or products in a way that allows the customer to access them in the most
terms.definition: Customer care refers to the practice that enables an organization to deliver services or products in a way that allows the customer to access them in the most (Health service management and entrepreneurship curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Use Customer care as a practical nursing topic, not only a memorized definition. Translate theory into safe decisions, accountability, communication and service improvement.

terms.simpleDefinition: Bluish discoloration of skin or mucous membranes from low oxygen.
terms.definition: Cyanosis is a clinical sign where the skin, lips or nail beds appear blue or dusky because blood oxygen is low.
terms.clinicalContext: Nurses treat cyanosis as an urgent warning sign and assess airway, breathing, circulation and oxygen saturation.
terms.example: In practice, nurses use the term cyanosis when assessing, documenting or explaining patient care.
terms.mnemonics: Connect the word to assessment, documentation and safe nursing action.

terms.simpleDefinition: Cystitis belongs to digestive and hepatobiliary nursing because it can affect nutrition, hydration, pain control, drug metabolism, elimination and infection prevention.
terms.definition: Cystitis belongs to digestive and hepatobiliary nursing because it can affect nutrition, hydration, pain control, drug metabolism, elimination and infection prevention. (Medical Nursing (ll) and Pharmacology (ll) curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Assess pain site and character, vomiting, stool changes, appetite, hydration, weight change, fever and abdominal distension.

terms.simpleDefinition: Painful symmetric non-pitting swelling of infant hands & feet — often the FIRST vaso-occlusive crisis presenting sign of Sickle Cell Disease around 6–12 months.
terms.definition: Painful symmetric non-pitting swelling of infant hands & feet — often the FIRST vaso-occlusive crisis presenting sign of Sickle Cell Disease around 6–12 months.
terms.clinicalContext: Screen infant haemoglobin electrophoresis / sickling test cleanly alongside hydration & gentle analgesia.

terms.simpleDefinition: Dangers of narcotics is a mental-health and safety topic because substance use or poisoning can affect judgement, behaviour, breathing, circulation, family wellbeing and long-term recovery.
terms.definition: Dangers of narcotics is a mental-health and safety topic because substance use or poisoning can affect judgement, behaviour, breathing, circulation, family wellbeing and long-term recovery. (Mental Health Nursing(II) Pharmacology (III) curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Dangers of narcotics is a mental-health and safety topic because substance use or poisoning can affect judgement, behaviour, breathing, circulation, family wellbeing and long-term recovery.

terms.simpleDefinition: Death is the cessation of life for an individual or organism.
terms.definition: Death is the cessation of life for an individual or organism. (Paediatric Nursing (i) curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Providing holistic care continues until the end of life and beyond. When necessary, seek assistance from other team members or organizations. There are different paths towards dying, and while most patients follow the.

terms.simpleDefinition: Blood clot inside deep leg veins (calf/femoral) causing unilateral warm swollen painful limb and life-threatening Pulmonary Embolism risk.
terms.definition: Blood clot inside deep leg veins (calf/femoral) causing unilateral warm swollen painful limb and life-threatening Pulmonary Embolism risk.
terms.clinicalContext: NEVER massage a suspected DVT calf; maintain bed rest temporarily, start prescribed heparin/anticoagulant, and watch for sudden pleuritic chest pain or dyspnoea (PE).

terms.term: Definition of terms used in medical nursing
terms.simpleDefinition: Definition of terms used in medical nursing gives the foundation for recognizing disease patterns early, preventing avoidable complications and planning nursing care that fits the patient's condition and home situation.
terms.definition: Definition of terms used in medical nursing gives the foundation for recognizing disease patterns early, preventing avoidable complications and planning nursing care that fits the patient's condition and home situation. (Medical Nursing (I) and Pharmacology (I) curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Start with airway, breathing, circulation, disability and exposure before moving to focused history.

terms.simpleDefinition: Dehiscence = partial/full separation of abdominal wound layers; Evisceration = loops of bowel protruding outside opened wound.
terms.definition: Dehiscence = partial/full separation of abdominal wound layers; Evisceration = loops of bowel protruding outside opened wound.
terms.clinicalContext: EVISCERATION EMERGENCY: Stay calm with patient, lie supine knees slightly bent to relax abdomen, cover protruding organs IMMEDIATELY with sterile warm 0.9% saline-soaked towels (NEVER push bowel back in!), keep NBM, call surgeon urgently.

terms.simpleDefinition: Too little water in the body.
terms.definition: Dehydration occurs when fluid loss is greater than fluid intake. It may follow vomiting, diarrhoea, fever, bleeding, poor intake or excessive sweating.
terms.clinicalContext: Nurses assess thirst, dry mucous membranes, reduced urine, low blood pressure, fast pulse, poor skin turgor and altered consciousness.
terms.example: In practice, nurses use the term dehydration when assessing, documenting or explaining patient care.
terms.mnemonics: Connect the word to assessment, documentation and safe nursing action.

terms.term: DELAYS IN SAFE MOTHERHOOD - Midwives Revision
terms.simpleDefinition: DELAYS IN SAFE MOTHERHOOD MEANS DEATH
terms.definition: DELAYS IN SAFE MOTHERHOOD MEANS DEATH (Gynaecology 1 and Reproductive Health 1 curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: As every mother has a right to conclude her pregnancy safely, so also the baby has a right to be born alive, safe and healthy. As such improvement of obstetric services will not minimize perinatal death appreciably.

terms.simpleDefinition: Delirium is ACUTE, fluctuating, reversible brain confusion (infection, hypoxia, drugs); Dementia is CHRONIC progressive memory/cognitive decline.
terms.definition: Delirium is ACUTE, fluctuating, reversible brain confusion (infection, hypoxia, drugs); Dementia is CHRONIC progressive memory/cognitive decline.
terms.clinicalContext: Always rule out hypoxia, UTI, hypoglycaemia, or sepsis first when an elderly patient develops sudden overnight confusion.

terms.simpleDefinition: Aedes mosquito-borne flavivirus causing abrupt high fever, severe retro-orbital headache, myalgia ('breakbone fever'), rash, and plasma-leakage shock warning.
terms.definition: Aedes mosquito-borne flavivirus causing abrupt high fever, severe retro-orbital headache, myalgia ('breakbone fever'), rash, and plasma-leakage shock warning.
terms.clinicalContext: Give Paracetamol ONLY — strictly AVOID Aspirin/Ibuprofen NSAIDs due to severe thrombocytopaenic haemorrhage risk!

terms.simpleDefinition: 150 mg IM (or Sayana Press SC) progestin-only injection given cleanly every 12 weeks (13 weeks grace window).
terms.definition: 150 mg IM (or Sayana Press SC) progestin-only injection given cleanly every 12 weeks (13 weeks grace window).
terms.clinicalContext: Counsel upfront on expected lighter/irregular spotting or amenorrhoea (does not hurt uterus!) and do NOT firmly massage injection site.

terms.simpleDefinition: Specific unilateral skin band strip supplied by a single spinal dorsal nerve root — key landmark in spinal anaesthesia height check & Shingles distribution.
terms.definition: Specific unilateral skin band strip supplied by a single spinal dorsal nerve root — key landmark in spinal anaesthesia height check & Shingles distribution.
terms.clinicalContext: Know key landmarks: T4 = Nipples, T10 = Umbilicus (used cleanly checking spinal block height before C-section!).

terms.simpleDefinition: Deficient ADH release or renal resistance pouring 4–15 L/day pale dilute urine (specific gravity < 1.005) -> severe hypernatraemia & thirst.
terms.definition: Deficient ADH release or renal resistance pouring 4–15 L/day pale dilute urine (specific gravity < 1.005) -> severe hypernatraemia & thirst.
terms.clinicalContext: Match strict hourly urine output with oral water/IV 5% Dextrose or Desmopressin cleanly.

terms.simpleDefinition: Type 1: autoimmune beta-cell destruction requiring lifelong insulin. Type 2: insulin resistance + progressive beta-cell fatigue.
terms.definition: Type 1: autoimmune beta-cell destruction requiring lifelong insulin. Type 2: insulin resistance + progressive beta-cell fatigue.
terms.clinicalContext: Check foot ulcers daily, teach sick-day insulin rules (never omit basal insulin even when vomiting — check RBG & ketones), and carry quick sugar.

terms.simpleDefinition: Stocking-glove peripheral nerve loss eliminating protective pain -> silent painless shoe trauma turning into deep limb-threatening ulcers.
terms.definition: Stocking-glove peripheral nerve loss eliminating protective pain -> silent painless shoe trauma turning into deep limb-threatening ulcers.
terms.clinicalContext: Perform 10g monofilament screening annually, inspect footwear/between toes daily, never walk barefoot, cut nails straight across.

terms.simpleDefinition: Life-threatening triad of hyperglycaemia, metabolic acidosis, and ketonaemia in insulin deficiency.
terms.definition: Triggers osmotic diuresis, severe dehydration, Kussmaul deep rapid breathing, fruity acetone breath, abdominal pain, and potassium shifts.
terms.clinicalContext: Priority sequence: 1) IV 0.9% Normal Saline resuscitation FIRST, 2) Fixed-rate IV Soluble Insulin infusion, 3) Monitor serum K+ closely BEFORE and DURING insulin therapy to avoid fatal hypokalaemia.

terms.simpleDefinition: Artificial blood filtration removing uraemic toxins and excess fluid/potassium when kidneys fail.
terms.definition: Artificial blood filtration removing uraemic toxins and excess fluid/potassium when kidneys fail.
terms.clinicalContext: Inspect AV fistula thrill/bruit daily, forbid BP cuffs/IVs on fistula arm, and weigh patient before & after each session.

terms.simpleDefinition: Watery loose stools >= 3/day; Dysentery features visible blood/mucus indicating invasive Shigella or Entamoeba histolytica.
terms.definition: Watery loose stools >= 3/day; Dysentery features visible blood/mucus indicating invasive Shigella or Entamoeba histolytica.
terms.clinicalContext: Always prescribe Zinc (20 mg daily x 10–14d; 10 mg if < 6 months) alongside low-osmolarity ORS; treat dysentery with Ciprofloxacin per UCG.

terms.simpleDefinition: Rapid mucosal rectal benzodiazepine route (0.5 mg/kg) halting active childhood seizures within 2–5 minutes when IV access is unavailable.
terms.definition: Rapid mucosal rectal benzodiazepine route (0.5 mg/kg) halting active childhood seizures within 2–5 minutes when IV access is unavailable.
terms.clinicalContext: Use needleless syringe 4–5 cm gently inside rectum, pinch buttocks smoothly 1–2 minutes post-instillation so medication stays absorbed cleanly, watch respiration.

terms.simpleDefinition: Different types of narcotics is a mental-health and safety topic because substance use or poisoning can affect judgement, behaviour, breathing, circulation, family wellbeing and long-term recovery.

terms.clinicalContext: Different types of narcotics is a mental-health and safety topic because substance use or poisoning can affect judgement, behaviour, breathing, circulation, family wellbeing and long-term recovery.

terms.definition: Digestive System Agents focuses on the systems that make medicine use safe: clear prescriptions, accurate calculations, correct storage, lawful supply, rational selection and careful administration. In Uganda, nurses. (Pharmacology I curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Digestive System Agents focuses on the systems that make medicine use safe: clear prescriptions, accurate calculations, correct storage, lawful supply, rational selection and careful administration. In Uganda, nurses.

terms.simpleDefinition: By the end of this unit, the student shall be able to:
terms.definition: By the end of this unit, the student shall be able to: (Anatomy & physiology 1 & First aid curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Use Digestive system as a practical nursing topic, not only a memorized definition. Prioritize airway, breathing, circulation, pain, asepsis, wound healing and early complication detection.

terms.simpleDefinition: Narrow-therapeutic-index toxicity precipitated by hypokalaemia or CKD causing nausea, yellow-green visual halos, and arrhythmias.
terms.definition: Narrow-therapeutic-index toxicity precipitated by hypokalaemia or CKD causing nausea, yellow-green visual halos, and arrhythmias.
terms.clinicalContext: Check full 1-minute apical pulse BEFORE every dose — HOLD if adult HR < 60 bpm (child < 80–90 bpm) and check serum K+.

terms.clinicalContext: Assess level of consciousness, orientation, pupils, limb strength, speech, swallowing, seizures, headache, neck stiffness and vital signs.

The nurse supports safety,. (Mental Health Nursing (I) and Pharmacology (II) curriculum concept).

terms.simpleDefinition: Genital ulcer disease is a common syndrome affecting both men and women, characterized by single or multiple ulcers with different clinical manifestations.
terms.definition: Genital ulcer disease is a common syndrome affecting both men and women, characterized by single or multiple ulcers with different clinical manifestations. (Gynecology & Reproductive health curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Prompt treatment is important due to the increased risk of HIV transmission associated with genital ulcers.

terms.simpleDefinition: Glucose intolerance diagnosed first in pregnancy risking fetal macrosomia (> 4 kg), shoulder dystocia, polyhydramnios, & newborn neonatal hypoglycaemia immediately at birth.
terms.definition: Glucose intolerance diagnosed first in pregnancy risking fetal macrosomia (> 4 kg), shoulder dystocia, polyhydramnios, & newborn neonatal hypoglycaemia immediately at birth.
terms.clinicalContext: Check neonate blood glucose at 1–2 hrs post-delivery and initiate immediate early feeding to prevent severe rebound neonatal hypoglycaemia.

terms.simpleDefinition: Painless fibrous gum overgrowth encasing teeth triggered by Phenytoin, Cyclosporine, or Nifedipine.
terms.definition: Painless fibrous gum overgrowth encasing teeth triggered by Phenytoin, Cyclosporine, or Nifedipine.
terms.clinicalContext: Teach thorough gentle twice-daily brushing, flossing, & routine dental cleanings rather than abrupt anti-epileptic stopping.

terms.simpleDefinition: Standardized 3–15 point neurological scale assessing Eye opening, Verbal response, and Motor response.
terms.definition: Scores Eye (1–4), Verbal (1–5), and Motor (1–6). GCS <=8 indicates severe coma and inability to protect the airway.
terms.clinicalContext: 'GCS 8 or less — Intubate / Secure Airway!' Always record component breakdown (e.g., E3 V4 M6 = 13/15) rather than only a total sum, and escalate any drop >=2 points immediately.
terms.mnemonics: Eyes 4, Verbal 5, Motor 6 = 15 max (8 or less = Coma).

terms.simpleDefinition: Optic nerve cupping/vision loss from raised intraocular pressure; Acute Angle-Closure is an emergency with stony hard red eye, severe brow ache, dilated non-reactive pupil, and halos.
terms.definition: Optic nerve cupping/vision loss from raised intraocular pressure; Acute Angle-Closure is an emergency with stony hard red eye, severe brow ache, dilated non-reactive pupil, and halos.
terms.clinicalContext: Avoid anticholinergics/mydriatics (Atropine) in narrow-angle glaucoma; start Pilocarpine, Acetazolamide, and Mannitol urgently as prescribed.

terms.simpleDefinition: Immune-complex glomerular injury post Group A Strep throat/impetigo causing dark smoky haematuria, periorbital oedema, and hypertension.
terms.definition: Immune-complex glomerular injury post Group A Strep throat/impetigo causing dark smoky haematuria, periorbital oedema, and hypertension.
terms.clinicalContext: Monitor strict blood pressure, fluid/salt restriction, daily weights, and hypertensive encephalopathy signs.

terms.simpleDefinition: Pancreatic alpha-cell hormone mobilizing hepatic glycogen stores within 10–15 min when unconscious hypoglycaemic diabetics lack IV access.
terms.definition: Pancreatic alpha-cell hormone mobilizing hepatic glycogen stores within 10–15 min when unconscious hypoglycaemic diabetics lack IV access.
terms.clinicalContext: Note Glucagon FAILS in depleted glycogen states (alcoholics, starvation, severe liver cirrhosis) — give IV Dextrose directly instead; once conscious give oral complex carbs!

terms.simpleDefinition: 75g fasting glucose challenge confirming Diabetes (2-hr >= 11.1 mmol/L) or Gestational Diabetes.
terms.definition: 75g fasting glucose challenge confirming Diabetes (2-hr >= 11.1 mmol/L) or Gestational Diabetes.
terms.clinicalContext: Patient remains seated resting fasting cleanly throughout the 2-hour test window.

terms.simpleDefinition: Potent volatile sublingual coronary vasodilator breaking acute angina attacks within 2–3 min.
terms.definition: Potent volatile sublingual coronary vasodilator breaking acute angina attacks within 2–3 min.
terms.clinicalContext: Store strictly inside original dark amber glass bottle away from light/heat (replace every 8–12 weeks once opened); sit patient down first & check BP >= 90 SBP.

terms.simpleDefinition: Presence of measurable glucose in urine when blood sugar exceeds renal threshold (~10 mmol/L).
terms.definition: Detected cleanly via urine reagent dipstick strips; hallmark screening finding in uncontrolled diabetes mellitus, gestational diabetes, or renal tubular dysfunction.
terms.clinicalContext: Any positive urine glucose must be followed with capillary random/fasting blood glucose testing and dipstick ketones check.

terms.simpleDefinition: Neck swelling of thyroid gland (iodine deficiency, Graves, multinodular); surgery carries hypocalcaemia & airway haematoma dangers.
terms.definition: Neck swelling of thyroid gland (iodine deficiency, Graves, multinodular); surgery carries hypocalcaemia & airway haematoma dangers.
terms.clinicalContext: Keep sterile tracheostomy tray, suction, & suture-removal kit beside bed 24–48 hrs post-thyroidectomy and watch for voice hoarseness or stridor.

terms.simpleDefinition: Gonadotropin drugs explained for mental-health nursing with medicine-safety checks, risk monitoring, adherence teaching and legal documentation priorities.
terms.definition: Gonadotropin drugs explained for mental-health nursing with medicine-safety checks, risk monitoring, adherence teaching and legal documentation priorities. (Mental Health Nursing(II) Pharmacology (III) curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Gonadotropin drugs connects medicine action to a specific body system. The nurse should review normal physiology first, then ask how each medicine changes that system and which observations prove benefit or harm.

terms.simpleDefinition: Gonorrhoea is a sexually transmitted infection caused by the Neisseria gonorrhoeae bacterium, which targets the mucous membranes of the reproductive tract.
terms.definition: Gonorrhoea is a sexually transmitted infection caused by the Neisseria gonorrhoeae bacterium, which targets the mucous membranes of the reproductive tract. (Gynecology & Reproductive health curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Untreated gonorrhoea can lead to severe permanent problems in both men and women, increasing the risk of acquiring HIV, hepatitis B and C.

terms.simpleDefinition: Uric acid crystal deposition causing excruciating hot red swelling typically of the first metatarsophalangeal big toe joint.
terms.definition: Uric acid crystal deposition causing excruciating hot red swelling typically of the first metatarsophalangeal big toe joint.
terms.clinicalContext: Treat acute flare with NSAID/Colchicine (never start Allopurinol abruptly mid-flare), push fluids, and restrict purine/alcohol intake.

terms.simpleDefinition: Autoimmune TSH-receptor antibodies hyperstimulating thyroid -> goitre bruit, weight loss with huge appetite, heat intolerance, fine tremor, & exophthalmos bulging eyes.
terms.definition: Autoimmune TSH-receptor antibodies hyperstimulating thyroid -> goitre bruit, weight loss with huge appetite, heat intolerance, fine tremor, & exophthalmos bulging eyes.
terms.clinicalContext: Protect exposed bulging dry eyes cleanly at night with lubricating ointment/tape and watch for Thyroid Storm.

terms.simpleDefinition: Obstetric shorthand recording total pregnancies (Gravida) and viable births >=28 weeks (Parity).
terms.definition: In Uganda's obstetric practice, viability is conventionally counted from 28 weeks gestation (or >1000 g); e.g., G3P2+0 means 3 pregnancies, 2 deliveries >=28 wks, 0 abortions/losses.
terms.clinicalContext: Grand multiparity (>=5 deliveries) carries elevated risk of uterine atony, malpresentation, and postpartum haemorrhage—actively prepare AMTSL and uterotonics.

terms.simpleDefinition: Growth in adolescence refers to the physical changes that occur during this period of development.
terms.definition: Growth in adolescence refers to the physical changes that occur during this period of development. (Gynecology & Reproductive health curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Use Development as a practical nursing topic, not only a memorized definition. Start with normal structure and function, then connect it to assessment findings and disease.

terms.definition: Growth is the process of physical increase in size, such as height and weight. It is a quantitative measure that also includes the maturation of body systems. (Pediatric nursing I & Palliative care nursing curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Use Child growth and development as a practical nursing topic, not only a memorized definition. Adapt assessment and care to age, weight, development, caregiver knowledge and family support.

terms.clinicalContext: Use Growth Monitoring and Promotion as a practical nursing topic, not only a memorized definition. Adapt assessment and care to age, weight, development, caregiver knowledge and family support.

terms.definition: Post-infectious ascending symmetrical motor weakness/areflexia risking rapid diaphragmatic respiratory failure.
terms.clinicalContext: Monitor serial Forced Vital Capacity / peak cough and prepare mechanical ventilation proactively BEFORE cyanosis occurs.

terms.simpleDefinition: Gynaecology is a branch of medicine which deals with diseases of the female reproductive systems.
terms.definition: Gynaecology is a branch of medicine which deals with diseases of the female reproductive systems. (Gynaecology (II) and Reproductive Health (II) curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Use Introduction to Gynaecology as a practical nursing topic, not only a memorized definition. Start with normal structure and function, then connect it to assessment findings and disease.

terms.simpleDefinition: Habitual abortion refers to the occurrence of spontaneous abortion in three or more consecutive pregnancies.
terms.definition: Habitual abortion refers to the occurrence of spontaneous abortion in three or more consecutive pregnancies. (Gynaecology 1 and Reproductive Health 1 curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Mothers should be referred to specialized clinics for screening services.

terms.simpleDefinition: Painful acute bleeding inside a joint capsule (knee/ankle/elbow) hallmark of severe Haemophilia A or B.
terms.definition: Painful acute bleeding inside a joint capsule (knee/ankle/elbow) hallmark of severe Haemophilia A or B.
terms.clinicalContext: Give clotting factor concentrate IMMEDIATELY (before ice/rest alone!), immobilize gently in mild flexion initially, NEVER use Aspirin.

terms.simpleDefinition: Haematemesis = vomiting bright red or 'coffee-ground' blood; Melaena = black tarry foul-smelling stool from upper GI bleeding (oesophageal varices/peptic ulcer).
terms.definition: Haematemesis = vomiting bright red or 'coffee-ground' blood; Melaena = black tarry foul-smelling stool from upper GI bleeding (oesophageal varices/peptic ulcer).
terms.clinicalContext: Two 16G IV lines, cross-match blood, high-dose IV PPI (Omeprazole) / Octreotide for varices, and prepare urgent endoscopy.

terms.simpleDefinition: Surgically joined forearm artery-to-vein conduit maturing for repetitive high-flow dialysis access.
terms.definition: Surgically joined forearm artery-to-vein conduit maturing for repetitive high-flow dialysis access.
terms.clinicalContext: Feel smooth buzzing 'thrill' & auscultate 'bruit' every shift; NEVER measure blood pressure, draw blood, or insert IVs in that arm ('No BP/IV Arm Band').

terms.simpleDefinition: X-linked congenital clotting Factor VIII (Haemophilia A) or IX (Haemophilia B) deficiency causing painful haemarthrosis & deep bleeds.
terms.definition: X-linked congenital clotting Factor VIII (Haemophilia A) or IX (Haemophilia B) deficiency causing painful haemarthrosis & deep bleeds.
terms.clinicalContext: Avoid Aspirin, NSAIDs, and IM injections; replace deficient Factor VIII/IX concentrate promptly before even minor procedures.

terms.simpleDefinition: Haemophilus influenzae is a gram-negative, cocco-bacillary, facultatively anaerobic bacterium that falls within the Coccobacilli group. While it normally

terms.clinicalContext: To minimize further complication.

terms.simpleDefinition: Coughing up blood or blood-stained sputum from the lower respiratory tract.
terms.definition: Key red-flag symptom in Pulmonary Tuberculosis (PTB), bronchiectasis, lung abscess, pulmonary embolism, or mitral stenosis; distinct from haematemesis (vomited GI blood).
terms.clinicalContext: Initiate airborne/droplet respiratory isolation precautions immediately if chronic cough >2 weeks + weight loss/night sweats is present, and send sputum GeneXpert / AFB.

terms.simpleDefinition: Haemoptysis = coughing bright red FROTHY alkaline blood mixed with sputum (TB, bronchiectasis, PE, lung CA); Haematemesis = vomiting dark acid 'coffee-ground' or clotted blood mixed with food.
terms.definition: Haemoptysis = coughing bright red FROTHY alkaline blood mixed with sputum (TB, bronchiectasis, PE, lung CA); Haematemesis = vomiting dark acid 'coffee-ground' or clotted blood mixed with food.

terms.simpleDefinition: Blood loss >=500 mL after vaginal delivery or >=1000 mL after Caesarean section.
terms.definition: Leading cause of maternal mortality worldwide; driven by the '4 Ts': Tone (uterine atony ~70%), Trauma (cervical/vaginal tears), Tissue (retained placenta), and Thrombin (coagulopathy).
terms.clinicalContext: Act immediately: Call for help, bimanual/fundal uterine massage, Oxytocin 10 IU IM/IV + 20–40 IU infusion, empty bladder, inspect tears, give Tranexamic acid 1 g IV within 3 hours.
terms.mnemonics: 4 Ts of PPH: Tone, Trauma, Tissue, Thrombin.

terms.clinicalContext: Haemorrhage, commonly known as bleeding, is the loss of blood from the circulatory system, specifically from blood vessels. It is a critical medical condition that, if uncontrolled, can lead to severe physiological.

terms.simpleDefinition: Collection of blood (haemothorax) or trapped air (pneumothorax) inside pleural space collapsing lung tissue.
terms.definition: Collection of blood (haemothorax) or trapped air (pneumothorax) inside pleural space collapsing lung tissue.

terms.definition: Hearing impairment is defined as an impairment in hearing, whether permanent or fluctuating, that adversely affects a person's ability to hear and understand (Paediatric Nursing (III) curriculum concept).

terms.definition: Life-threatening severe pre-eclampsia variant: Haemolysis, Elevated Liver enzymes, Low Platelets.

terms.definition: Unconsciousness (Coma) is a neurological nursing topic because it can affect consciousness, movement, speech, swallowing, breathing, safety, infection risk and long-term function. (Medical Nursing (ll) and Pharmacology (ll) curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Assess level of consciousness, orientation, pupils, limb strength, speech, swallowing, seizures, headache, neck stiffness and vital signs.

terms.simpleDefinition: Under water seal drainage is a system that allows drainage of the pleural space using an airtight system to maintain sub-atmospheric intrapleural pressure.
terms.definition: Under water seal drainage is a system that allows drainage of the pleural space using an airtight system to maintain sub-atmospheric intrapleural pressure. (Foundations of Nursing (III) curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Use Under Water Seal Drainage as a practical nursing topic, not only a memorized definition. Turn the topic into practical nursing knowledge: meaning, assessment, care priorities, teaching and evaluation.

terms.simpleDefinition: An Upper Respiratory Tract Infection (URTI), commonly referred to as "the common cold", is a symptom complex primarily caused by viruses, occasionally bacteria, and very rarely fungi.
terms.definition: An Upper Respiratory Tract Infection (URTI), commonly referred to as "the common cold", is a symptom complex primarily caused by viruses, occasionally bacteria, and very rarely fungi. (Microbiology curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Use Upper Respiratory Tract Infections (URTIs) as a practical nursing topic, not only a memorized definition. Link cause, transmission, incubation, clinical features, treatment support and prevention.

terms.simpleDefinition: Toxic clinical syndrome in severe kidney failure featuring nausea, metallic taste, pruritus, asterixis flap, pericardial friction rub, and encephalopathy.
terms.definition: Toxic clinical syndrome in severe kidney failure featuring nausea, metallic taste, pruritus, asterixis flap, pericardial friction rub, and encephalopathy.
terms.clinicalContext: Monitor pericardial friction rub (dialysis urgency), fluid overload, and neurological changes.

terms.simpleDefinition: Urethral discharge syndrome is a prevalent sexually transmitted infection (STI) among men, marked by purulent urethral discharge, with or without dysuria.
terms.definition: Urethral discharge syndrome is a prevalent sexually transmitted infection (STI) among men, marked by purulent urethral discharge, with or without dysuria. (Gynecology & Reproductive health curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: All male patients with urethral discharge should be managed according to the syndromic chart.

terms.simpleDefinition: Urethritis belongs to digestive and hepatobiliary nursing because it can affect nutrition, hydration, pain control, drug metabolism, elimination and infection prevention.
terms.definition: Urethritis belongs to digestive and hepatobiliary nursing because it can affect nutrition, hydration, pain control, drug metabolism, elimination and infection prevention. (Medical Nursing (ll) and Pharmacology (ll) curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Assess pain site and character, vomiting, stool changes, appetite, hydration, weight change, fever and abdominal distension.

terms.simpleDefinition: Welcome to the comprehensive master guide on Urinary Tract Infections (UTIs). This guide covers everything from the microscopic battleground between bacterial
terms.definition: Welcome to the comprehensive master guide on Urinary Tract Infections (UTIs). This guide covers everything from the microscopic battleground between bacterial (Microbiology curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Use Urinary Tract Infections (UTIs) as a practical nursing topic, not only a memorized definition. Link cause, transmission, incubation, clinical features, treatment support and prevention.

terms.simpleDefinition: Failure of uterine myometrial muscles to contract firmly after childbirth, leaving a soft boggy uterus.
terms.definition: Permits rapid torrential bleeding from open placental-site spiral arteries; accounts for ~70% of primary postpartum haemorrhage cases.
terms.clinicalContext: Prevent routinely with Active Management of Third Stage of Labour (Oxytocin 10 IU IM within 1 minute of birth); feel abdomen immediately postpartum—boggy = massage + uterotonics!

terms.simpleDefinition: Causes of uterine fibroids are not fully understood, but research suggests that hormones and genetics play significant roles in their development.
terms.definition: Causes of uterine fibroids are not fully understood, but research suggests that hormones and genetics play significant roles in their development. (Gynaecology (II) and Reproductive Health (II) curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Most fibroids do not require treatment unless they are causing symptoms. After menopause, fibroids usually shrink, and it is unusual for fibroids to cause problems. The choice of management depends on several factors:

terms.simpleDefinition: Inversion: uterus turns inside-out during unguarded traction causing severe vagal/neurogenic shock; Rupture: torn uterine wall (scar/obstructed labour) causing sudden sharp pain loss, cessation of contractions, easily felt fetal parts, & absent FHR.
terms.definition: Inversion: uterus turns inside-out during unguarded traction causing severe vagal/neurogenic shock; Rupture: torn uterine wall (scar/obstructed labour) causing sudden sharp pain loss, cessation of contractions, easily felt fetal parts, & absent FHR.
terms.clinicalContext: For rupture -> urgent laparotomy; for inversion -> leave placenta attached initially if still adherent, push fundus gently upward via Johnson's manoeuvre, start Oxytocin only AFTER replacement.

terms.term: Uterus, Fallopian tubes and Ovaries - Midwives Revision
terms.simpleDefinition: The uterus is a hollow muscular organ of the female reproductive system where offspring gestate.A pear-shaped organ, the uterus lies posterior-superior to the
terms.definition: The uterus is a hollow muscular organ of the female reproductive system where offspring gestate.A pear-shaped organ, the uterus lies posterior-superior to the (Obstetrical anatomy curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Use Uterus, Uterine tubes and Ovaries as a practical nursing topic, not only a memorized definition. Read the topic through the safety of two patients: the mother and the fetus or newborn.

terms.simpleDefinition: Vaccines are special preparations of antigenic materials that can be used to stimulate the development of antibodies and thus confer active immunity against a
terms.definition: Vaccines are special preparations of antigenic materials that can be used to stimulate the development of antibodies and thus confer active immunity against a (Mental Health and Pharmacology ii curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Use Vaccines and Immunoglobulins) as a practical nursing topic, not only a memorized definition. Read the topic through the safety of two patients: the mother and the fetus or newborn.

terms.simpleDefinition: 4-hourly active-labour pelvic check assessing cervical dilation (0–10 cm), effacement, station (-3 to +3), moulding, membranes, and cord exclusion.
terms.definition: 4-hourly active-labour pelvic check assessing cervical dilation (0–10 cm), effacement, station (-3 to +3), moulding, membranes, and cord exclusion.
terms.clinicalContext: Contraindicated STRICTLY in antepartum haemorrhage until ultrasound rules out placenta praevia; minimize after membrane rupture.

terms.simpleDefinition: Highly infectious airborne & contact herpesvirus rash with concurrent 'crops' of macules, papules, vesicles ('dewdrop on rose petal'), and crusts.
terms.definition: Highly infectious airborne & contact herpesvirus rash with concurrent 'crops' of macules, papules, vesicles ('dewdrop on rose petal'), and crusts.
terms.clinicalContext: Isolate away from pregnant mothers and immunocompromised children; trim fingernails to prevent secondary Group A Strep skin superinfection.

terms.simpleDefinition: Severe ischaemic pain crisis when sickled red blood cells block small capillaries in bones or organs.
terms.definition: Triggered in Sickle Cell Disease (HbSS) by dehydration, hypoxia, cold weather, or infections (malaria/pneumonia), presenting as dactylitis, long bone pain, or acute chest syndrome.
terms.clinicalContext: Priority triage triad: 1) Rapid IV/oral Hydration, 2) Adequate stepped Analgesia (Paracetamol + Ibuprofen/Morphine—never delay opioids!), 3) Oxygen + keep warm + treat infection.

terms.simpleDefinition: Venous = medial malleolus gaiter area, warm skin, haemosiderin brown staining, irregular wet shallow base, milder pain better elevated. Arterial = lateral/toes punched-out deep pale cold painful base, absent pulse, worse elevated.
terms.definition: Venous = medial malleolus gaiter area, warm skin, haemosiderin brown staining, irregular wet shallow base, milder pain better elevated. Arterial = lateral/toes punched-out deep pale cold painful base, absent pulse, worse elevated.
terms.clinicalContext: Check Ankle-Brachial Pressure Index (ABPI) >= 0.8 BEFORE applying ANY compression bandage so you never gangrene an arterial leg.

terms.simpleDefinition: Colour-coded air-entrainment mask delivering exact fixed FiO2 (Blue 24%, White 28%, Yellow 35%, Red 40%, Green 60%) independent of patient breathing depth.
terms.definition: Colour-coded air-entrainment mask delivering exact fixed FiO2 (Blue 24%, White 28%, Yellow 35%, Red 40%, Green 60%) independent of patient breathing depth.
terms.clinicalContext: Essential oxygen mask for COPD retainers requiring exact 24%–28% controlled titration without hypercapnic narcosis.

terms.term: Violence and aggression of patients / clients
terms.simpleDefinition: Violence and aggression of patients / clients is a psychiatric emergency or high-risk mental-health topic. Nursing care prioritises immediate safety, calm assessment, de-escalation, observation, emergency referral and.
terms.definition: Violence and aggression of patients / clients is a psychiatric emergency or high-risk mental-health topic. Nursing care prioritises immediate safety, calm assessment, de-escalation, observation, emergency referral and. (Mental Health and Pharmacology ii curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Violence and aggression of patients / clients is a psychiatric emergency or high-risk mental-health topic. Nursing care prioritises immediate safety, calm assessment, de-escalation, observation, emergency referral and.

terms.simpleDefinition: Visual impairment also known as vision impairment or vision loss , is a decreased ability to see to a degree that causes problems not fixable by usual
terms.definition: Visual impairment also known as vision impairment or vision loss , is a decreased ability to see to a degree that causes problems not fixable by usual (Paediatric Nursing (III) curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Management ranges from Surgery, Pharmacological, Rehabilitation and Prevention.

terms.simpleDefinition: Temp 36.2–37.4 C · Pulse 60–100 bpm · RR 12–20 breaths/min · BP < 120/80 mmHg · SpO2 95–100%.
terms.definition: Temp 36.2–37.4 C · Pulse 60–100 bpm · RR 12–20 breaths/min · BP < 120/80 mmHg · SpO2 95–100%.
terms.clinicalContext: A sudden shift in trend across two consecutive charts matters even more than a single borderline number.

terms.simpleDefinition: Single 1 mg IM dose (0.5 mg < 1.5 kg) into anterolateral thigh at birth preventing fatal Haemorrhagic Disease of the Newborn.
terms.definition: Single 1 mg IM dose (0.5 mg < 1.5 kg) into anterolateral thigh at birth preventing fatal Haemorrhagic Disease of the Newborn.
terms.clinicalContext: Give cleanly within 1st hour post-delivery; vitamin K is poorly transferred across placenta and low in newborn gut flora.

terms.term: VULNERABLE GROUPS IN ADOLOSCENT REPRODUCTIVE HEALTH
terms.simpleDefinition: Vulnerable groups in Adolescent Reproductive Health Services are populations or individuals who face risks, challenges, or barriers in accessing and utilizing
terms.definition: Vulnerable groups in Adolescent Reproductive Health Services are populations or individuals who face risks, challenges, or barriers in accessing and utilizing (Gynecology & Reproductive health curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Use Vulnerable groups as a practical nursing topic, not only a memorized definition. Start with normal structure and function, then connect it to assessment findings and disease.

terms.simpleDefinition: Waste is any material – solid, liquid, or gas – that is unwanted and/or unvalued, and has been discarded or discharged by its owner.
terms.definition: Waste is any material – solid, liquid, or gas – that is unwanted and/or unvalued, and has been discarded or discharged by its owner. (Community health and Occupational health and safety curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Waste is any material – solid, liquid, or gas – that is unwanted and/or unvalued, and has been discarded or discharged by its owner .

terms.simpleDefinition: Acute reversible Thiamine (Vitamin B1) brain deficiency in chronic alcohol use/malnutrition causing triad: confusion, ataxia, and ophthalmoplegia/nystagmus.
terms.definition: Acute reversible Thiamine (Vitamin B1) brain deficiency in chronic alcohol use/malnutrition causing triad: confusion, ataxia, and ophthalmoplegia/nystagmus.
terms.clinicalContext: ALWAYS administer IV Thiamine BEFORE IV Dextrose infusion so glucose metabolism doesn't exhaust residual thiamine and precipitate permanent Korsakoff psychosis.

terms.simpleDefinition: Safe crutch fit: 2–3 fingerbreadths gap below axilla (weight borne strictly on HANDS, never armpits -> avoids radial nerve crutch palsy!).
terms.definition: Safe crutch fit: 2–3 fingerbreadths gap below axilla (weight borne strictly on HANDS, never armpits -> avoids radial nerve crutch palsy!).
terms.clinicalContext: Remember safety mnemonic going up/down stairs on crutches: 'Up with the Good leg, Down with the Bad leg'.

terms.simpleDefinition: Continuous high-pitched musical whistling sounds predominantly on EXPIRATION from narrowed small airways.
terms.definition: Indicates bronchospasm, airway oedema, or mucus plugging in bronchial asthma, infant bronchiolitis, COPD, or anaphylaxis.
terms.clinicalContext: A sudden 'SILENT CHEST' with poor air entry in severe asthma means extreme danger (exhaustion/imminent arrest), NOT improvement!

terms.simpleDefinition: Agglutination serology detecting Salmonella typhi antibodies; limited specificity in endemic Uganda due to prior vaccination, cross-reactivity, or past infection.
terms.definition: Agglutination serology detecting Salmonella typhi antibodies; limited specificity in endemic Uganda due to prior vaccination, cross-reactivity, or past infection.
terms.clinicalContext: Never over-diagnose Typhoid solely from an isolated weak Widal titre; interpret against fever history, blood/stool culture, and alternative causes like Malaria.

terms.simpleDefinition: Will: This document expresses the desires of a person regarding the distribution of their property among specific individuals or parties after their demise.
terms.definition: Will: This document expresses the desires of a person regarding the distribution of their property among specific individuals or parties after their demise. (Palliative Care Nursing curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Use Will Making as a practical nursing topic, not only a memorized definition. Focus on comfort, dignity, symptom control, communication and family support.

terms.simpleDefinition: Work-related injuries and fatalities are any injuries or deaths that occur as a result of work activities. They can be caused by a variety of factors,
terms.definition: Work-related injuries and fatalities are any injuries or deaths that occur as a result of work activities. They can be caused by a variety of factors, (Community health and Occupational health and safety curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Nurses are at risk of a range of work-related injuries and fatalities, both physical and psychological. Some of the most common types include:

terms.simpleDefinition: Workers' compensation is a system that provides cash and non-cash payments to individuals who have suffered loss, suffering, or injury while on the job.
terms.definition: Workers' compensation is a system that provides cash and non-cash payments to individuals who have suffered loss, suffering, or injury while on the job. (Community health and Occupational health and safety curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Use Workers compensation Act as a practical nursing topic, not only a memorized definition. Combine safety, therapeutic communication, mental status assessment and dignity.

terms.simpleDefinition: A break or injury in body tissue.
terms.definition: A wound may involve skin, mucous membrane or deeper tissue. It can result from surgery, trauma, pressure, burns or disease.
terms.clinicalContext: Nurses assess wound size, depth, edges, exudate, odour, pain, surrounding skin and signs of infection.
terms.example: In practice, nurses use the term wound when assessing, documenting or explaining patient care.
terms.mnemonics: Connect the word to assessment, documentation and safe nursing action.

terms.simpleDefinition: Partial or complete separation/bursting open of previously sutured surgical wound edges.
terms.definition: Often heralded on postoperative days 5–8 by sudden gush of serosanguinous ('pink watery') fluid; if viscera protrude through fascia, it is called EVISCERATION.
terms.clinicalContext: In Evisceration: STAY CALM, call surgeon stat, do NOT push organs back in—cover viscera with sterile saline-soaked gauze, bend patient's knees slightly (low-Fowler's), keep NBM.

terms.simpleDefinition: Wound dressing is a method of carrying out surgical dressing and operative treatment with an aim to prevent the entry of Microorganisms into the wound.
terms.definition: Wound dressing is a method of carrying out surgical dressing and operative treatment with an aim to prevent the entry of Microorganisms into the wound. (Foundations of nursing II, Sociology and psychology curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: Wound care is the planned assessment, cleaning, protection and monitoring of damaged tissue so healing occurs without avoidable infection or breakdown.

terms.simpleDefinition: Common radiographic imaging assessing lungs, heart silhouette, ribs, pneumothorax, and ETT/NGT positions.
terms.definition: Reveals lobar consolidation, pleural effusion meniscus, tension pneumothorax tracheal shift, cardiomegaly, and tuberculosis apical cavities.
terms.clinicalContext: Always verify pregnancy status BEFORE abdominal/pelvic X-rays in reproductive-age women and apply lead shielding when clinically feasible.

terms.simpleDefinition: Yellow bilirubin discolouration of centrifuged cerebrospinal fluid confirming Subarachnoid Haemorrhage (SAH) > 6–12 hours post-bleed vs traumatic tap.
terms.definition: Yellow bilirubin discolouration of centrifuged cerebrospinal fluid confirming Subarachnoid Haemorrhage (SAH) > 6–12 hours post-bleed vs traumatic tap.
terms.clinicalContext: Observe acute 'thunderclap' worst-ever headache + photophobia + neck stiffness for urgent CT head & neurosurgical care.

terms.simpleDefinition: Dry ocular keratinization and foamy white triangular Bitot's spots on conjunctiva pathognomonic for severe Vitamin A deficiency.
terms.definition: Dry ocular keratinization and foamy white triangular Bitot's spots on conjunctiva pathognomonic for severe Vitamin A deficiency.
terms.clinicalContext: Give therapeutic high-dose Vitamin A immediately + repeated at Day 2 and Week 2 to rescue vision cleanly.

terms.simpleDefinition: Abnormal dry mouth from anticholinergics, head-neck radiation, dehydration, or Sjogren's impairing swallowing, dentures, and dental hygiene.
terms.definition: Abnormal dry mouth from anticholinergics, head-neck radiation, dehydration, or Sjogren's impairing swallowing, dentures, and dental hygiene.
terms.clinicalContext: Offer frequent small sips of water, sugar-free lozenges, gentle soft moist brushing, and non-alcohol mouth care.

terms.simpleDefinition: Acute viral haemorrhagic disease transmitted by daytime-biting Aedes aegypti mosquitoes.
terms.definition: Features acute fever, severe backache, bradycardia-fever dissociation (Faget's sign), progressing in severe toxic phase to jaundice, haematemesis ('black vomit'), and renal failure.
terms.clinicalContext: Single lifetime Yellow Fever vaccine (Stamaril) confers lifelong immunity at >=99%; immediate notifiable viral haemorrhagic surveillance alert in Uganda.

terms.simpleDefinition: Yellow fever is an acute viral hemorrhagic disease transmitted by infected mosquitoes.
terms.definition: Yellow fever is an acute viral hemorrhagic disease transmitted by infected mosquitoes. (Midwifery II & Tropical medicine curriculum concept).
terms.clinicalContext: The primary aims of management are:

terms.simpleDefinition: Zoonotic Gram-negative coccobacillus (flea vector / rodent host in West Nile endemic foci) causing acute painful buboes or lethal pneumonic plague.
terms.definition: Zoonotic Gram-negative coccobacillus (flea vector / rodent host in West Nile endemic foci) causing acute painful buboes or lethal pneumonic plague.
terms.clinicalContext: Immediately isolate suspected pneumonic cases under strict droplet IPC, notify District Surveillance Focal Person cleanly, and initiate Doxycycline/Gentamicin/Streptomycin per MoH.

terms.simpleDefinition: Essential trace-mineral epithelial repair co-therapy cutting duration and severity of childhood diarrhoea by ~25% and preventing recurrence for 2–3 months.
terms.definition: Essential trace-mineral epithelial repair co-therapy cutting duration and severity of childhood diarrhoea by ~25% and preventing recurrence for 2–3 months.
terms.clinicalContext: Administer 20 mg once daily x 10–14 days for children >= 6 months (10 mg/day for infants < 6 months) dissolved in clean water or breastmilk.

terms.simpleDefinition: Essential WHO adjunct therapy given alongside ORS for acute childhood diarrhoea.
terms.definition: Dispersible Zinc sulphate (20 mg once daily for 10–14 days in children >=6 months; 10 mg if <6 months) restores intestinal mucosal brush border and reduces episode severity/recurrence.
terms.clinicalContext: Give strictly WITH ORS (never as a standalone replacement for fluids!) and advise mothers to finish the full 10-day course even after diarrhoea stops.

terms.simpleDefinition: Any infectious disease naturally transmitted between vertebrate animals and humans (Rabies, Brucellosis, Anthrax, Rift Valley Fever, Ebola/Marburg).
terms.definition: Any infectious disease naturally transmitted between vertebrate animals and humans (Rabies, Brucellosis, Anthrax, Rift Valley Fever, Ebola/Marburg).
terms.clinicalContext: Always ask animal contact, raw unpasteurized milk (Brucellosis), and bushmeat/slaughter exposures during fever workups.

terms.simpleDefinition: Diploid single-cell embryo formed by fusion of sperm and ovum inside the Fallopian ampulla, dividing toward morula and blastocyst before uterine implantation.
terms.definition: Diploid single-cell embryo formed by fusion of sperm and ovum inside the Fallopian ampulla, dividing toward morula and blastocyst before uterine implantation.
terms.clinicalContext: Remember early embryonic organogenesis peaks Weeks 3–8 — the highest vulnerability window for teratogenic drugs and rubella.
